title: Product Reliability at Palantir: Life on the PRX team
description: Palantir’s Product Reliability (PRX) team reflects on their work as Product Reliability Engineers (PREs) and Product Reliability Operations Analysts (PROs)
author: Palantir
body: Engineering Product Reliability Palantir Teams Palantir Culture Product Reliability at Palantir: Life on the PRX team Palantir 7 min read · Dec 15, 2021 -- Listen Share Editor’s Note: In this blog post, Product Reliability Engineers (PREs) and Product Reliability Operations Analysts (PROs) share what it’s like to work on Palantir’s Product Reliability (PRX) team. Press enter or click to view image in full size Palantir’s Gotham and Foundry platforms underpin mission-critical infrastructure throughout the world, whether they’re being used to deliver food assistance to remote corners of the world, increase aircraft production rates , or combat the COVID-19 pandemic . The Product Reliability (PRX) team drives stability across our products by ensuring uninterrupted customer access to Palantir platforms. Comprised of Product Reliability Engineers and Product Reliability Operations Analysts, PRX proactively and responsively assesses and addresses issues, from root causing, monitoring, and ultimately eliminating causes of instability. What does the Product Reliability team do? Product Reliability Engineers Product Reliability Engineers are the first line of defense when something goes wrong. PREs are responsible for triaging, troubleshooting, and coordinating the resolution of issues. They don’t just seek one-time fixes; PREs are essential to building permanent technical solutions and often embed with specific product teams to dive deep into product issues Product Reliability Operations Analysts Delivering stable and reliable products to customers requires robust operational infrastructure and processes. That’s where Product Reliability Operations Analysts (PROs) come in. PROs partner with teams across the business to scale and eliminate risks rooted in internal procedures. PROs own outcomes from Day 1. Across product release management, incident response, customer facing support, and cloud operations, PROs design, operate, and optimize the processes and solutions that Palantir relies on to deliver products and support to our customers. What does a typical day on PRX look like? Cecelia (PRE, New York) No two days are the same as a PRE, but the one commonality is that every day I’m focused on improving the stability of my team’s products. I spend time responding to support issues from other engineers and analyzing long-term stability trends for my team. I also contribute to bigger projects with a stability focus. Sometimes this means getting my hands dirty with technical contributions. Other times, I provide the operational support necessary to drive projects forward, creating project plans and ensuring stakeholders are aligned on the outcomes. Jacob (PRE, London) My job is to make sure my team is constantly improving the stability and performance of the products we manage. I look at trends in the issues we’re seeing in production, respond to support requests, and run incident retrospectives. I also make sure that the outcomes of all those actions are handled effectively. Being a PRE also means being an Incident Manager for emergencies that arise with our products, helping get those problems solved as quickly as possible. Julia (PRE, Denver) As the lead of the Incident Response Team, a typical day involves managing the team’s workload by meeting with stakeholders about the status of our projects and understanding what we need in order to be successful. I also spend time planning what the team will tackle over the next few months and brainstorming how to accomplish that, which is a part of my job I value because it allows me to understand the business outcomes of my team’s work. And I usually have a few 1:1 catchups with team members to see how they’re doing and how I can unblock them. Ed (PRO, New York) There truly isn’t a “typical day” as a PRO. You might be finding points of friction in support workflows, crafting automations, developing metrics, or planning projects to solve complex issues that internal teams are dealing with. But everything I work on relates to supporting other teams with their operational workflows, and has a positive impact on how other teams are able to be efficient in their work. Anne (PRO, Amsterdam) Some days I work independently, while others I collaborate with people across our Product and Business Development teams. This year, I’ve worked on our Stability team to analyze the root causes of Palantir incidents and advise our Foundry teams on the most effective investments to make to improve the stability of the platform. Some of this work is independent, like building models to analyze our outage data, but a lot of it involves collaboration with other teams. I might discuss my findings and strategies with the platform stability working group, present our advice to relevant product teams, or validate whether the investments we have made have improved user experience and platform stability. What does growth look like in Product Reliability? Cecelia (PRE, New York) Product Reliability has offered me the materials I need to “level up” my technical skills at every turn, whether through mentorship from a team member on how to approach a tough problem or a week-long course on a technical subject. I’ve also grown from a strategic perspective — getting a bird’s-eye view of the stability landscape has allowed me to become more opinionated on the pressing needs of the business and drive those outcomes to completion. Get Palantir ’s stories in your inbox Join Medium for free to get updates from this writer. Subscribe Subscribe Remember me for faster sign in Anne (PRO, Amsterdam) Growth at Palantir is choose-your-own-adventure, and Product Reliability is no exception. On Product Reliability, we are regularly exposed to new responsibilities and new projects through our work with product teams and dedicated task forces. In my own journey, my lead helped me identify how to be more effective and maximize my impact by finding opportunities that best align with my strengths. Jacob (PRE, London) For me, growth has looked like gaining sharper analytical skills and becoming more confident about making high-level decisions for the teams I’m involved with. I’ve also grown in technical ability. During my time as a PRE, I’ve learned so much more about not just the database technologies my team works with but also about software development in general. By working with a number of different dev teams across both Gotham and Foundry, I’ve gained a holistic understanding of how our products work and what they actually do, which in turn has provided me with experience and understanding that I bring into each new project. Julia (PRE, Denver) Growth in PRX can take many different forms based on your interests and skillsets. I started my career working on our Gotham platform, then moved to one of our Business Development teams to tackle stability issues that come with managing customer environments. I grew in my responsibilities as an individual contributor by taking on mentorship and becoming an interviewer. Over time, this led me naturally toward becoming a “people lead,” or Palantir’s version of manager, and later a team lead of the Incident Response Team. What do you like most about your role? Jacob (PRE, London) I enjoy the sense of ownership and agency around the work that I do. As a PRE, when I’m given a problem to solve, I’m not told how to solve that problem — most of the time, it’s a problem that hasn’t even been solved before. I have the freedom to decide how to best take the challenge on and the trust from my team that I’m doing the right thing. Granted, I don’t always do the right thing, but even then, I always know that my team has my back and that I’ll be able to learn and grow from the experience. Cecelia (PRE, New York) My favorite thing about PRX — and Palantir — is the people. I’m constantly surrounded by some of the smartest and most motivated people I’ve ever met, and the community is incredibly friendly and collaborative. I also like that I get to grow technically in a fast-paced environment. In addition to solving technical problems, I also get insight into many different facets of the business and feel like I get to do a little bit of everything. Julia (PRE, Denver) I love the variety of problems I get to work on. I truly feel like I could never get bored on PRX because there are constantly new challenges being thrown at our team. We touch every edge of the business, so I feel I could always find something new and exciting to work on. No day is ever the same at Palantir! Anne (PRO, Amsterdam) What I like best at Palantir is the people. People at Palantir come from a myriad of different backgrounds and everyone has their own story of how they ended up here. But what they all have in common is that they are really motivated and they really care. On PRX, you get to work with teams across the company, from product to business development to our internal teams. You get to see things from different perspectives and collaborate with people from across the business. Ed (PRO, New York) I came to Palantir because I wanted to help people, and the PRO role affords me the opportunity to help not just our customers but our internal teams as well. The problems I solve on a daily basis have variety, are challenging, and impact the company as a whole. I’m not stuck doing “busy work;” most of my time is spent tackling difficult issues, understanding what the root problem is, and then creating a standardized workflow or automating away the points of friction. This gives me a lot of satisfaction because I get to see the actual outcomes that I’m improving. Final Thoughts PRX sits at the heart of Palantir’s product and production operations, and we hope this post highlights some of the benefits of working on the team. If you’re passionate about product reliability and want a front row seat to the outcomes Palantir is driving everyday around the world, consider applying to one of our open roles: Product Reliability Engineers (PREs) Product Reliability Operations Analysts (PROs) Not sure about which role is best for you? Don’t worry — our recruiting team and interviewers will help you navigate the process to ensure that you’ll land in a role you can own from day one. And whatever role you end up in, you’ll work with teams across Product Development and Business Development to ensure that Palantir’s users have the platforms they need 24/7/365.

title: For Green and Equitable Roadways: Introducing the EV Infrastructure OS
description: The electrification of America with EV charge stations is the next revolution in mobility. How can we ensure EV infrastructure is efficient and sustainable?
author: Palantir
body: Electric Vehicles Palantirglobal Automotive Palantir Infrastructure For Green and Equitable Roadways: Introducing the EV Infrastructure OS Palantir 3 min read · Jan 11, 2022 -- Listen Share Press enter or click to view image in full size The electrification of America with Electric Vehicle (EV) charging stations could be the greatest investment in mobility infrastructure in the country since the construction of the Interstate Highway System in the mid 20th century. Through their construction and beyond, interstate highways expanded the potential of the personal vehicle, making it a ubiquitous part of American life. Today’s emerging grid of charging stations promises to do the same for the EV. With robust and far-reaching charging networks, EVs could one day inherit and push forward the legacy of American car culture — the long road trips that enable commerce and bring people together, and the horizon of opportunity provided by the freedom to go anywhere, cheaply and safely, at any time. Half a century later, the flaws and shortcomings of the Interstate Highway system have been extensively studied. The standardized federal project often collided with local conditions, erasing entire urban neighborhoods while leading to the decline of many other communities underserved by the road network. Charging networks and EVs offer the promise of clean and cheap transportation, but as massive infrastructure projects, they present both old and new problems that require innovative solutions. To empower businesses and organizations to take on these challenges, Palantir has unveiled the EV Infrastructure Operating System (OS), an application that can help ensure that future investments in EV infrastructure are efficient, equitable, and sustainable. Get Palantir ’s stories in your inbox Join Medium for free to get updates from this writer. Subscribe Subscribe Remember me for faster sign in Unlike the federal project of the Interstate Highway System, the electrification of American roads requires a new platform to enable decentralized, public-private collaboration involving many different stakeholders — from energy utilities and city authorities to network operators, retailers, and more. Charging networks also need to be built in response to local conditions, and to provide equitable access to the benefits of electric mobility. With its ability to layer multiple internal and external sources of data under a single operating picture, the EV Infrastructure OS can make this vision a reality. Press enter or click to view image in full size The OS integrates internal, open source, and 3rd party data through Palantir Foundry for operational decision-making, with the option to add Wejo’s robust connected vehicle data — including billions of near-real-time data points. Together, Palantir’s software and Wejo’s data enable companies to expand into new geographies and manage infrastructure through an integrated platform for optimal decision-making. With advanced site selection and network operations tools, any business or organization can use the OS to build, scale, and operate first-class EV charging infrastructure. Press enter or click to view image in full size The site selection workflow can help customers locate sites for chargers in areas where EV charging demand is greatest. The workflow enables users to optimize their site selection for charger utilization, and can also help determine the size, type, and kWh capacity per charger. After charging site installation, the app’s network operations tools help maximize revenue and increase network reliability. Be a part of this revolution today. Learn more about our latest offering and its features by downloading the whitepaper below.

title: Palantir: spørsmål og svar
description: Palantir er et programvareselskap som utvikler og lisensierer programvare som gjør det mulig for våre kunder å få bedre oversikt over sine…
author: Palantir
body: Palantir: spørsmål og svar Palantir er et programvareselskap som utvikler og lisensierer programvare som gjør det mulig for våre kunder å få bedre oversikt over sine egne data og gjennom dette ta klokere beslutninger. Vår forretningsmodell er ikke basert på innsamling eller salg av kundedata. Blant kundene våre finnes blant annet store, børsnoterte selskaper og offentlige virksomheter innen for eksempel helse, kraftproduksjon og annen infrastruktur. I noen land bistår vi også politi og andre myndighetsinstanser som skal sørge for at lover og regler blir fulgt og folks sikkerhet blir ivaretatt. Felles for alle våre produkter og prosjekter er at de er underlagt strenge personvernregler og bestemmelser om datasikkerhet. For noen av våre kunder, spesielt innen sikkerhetstjenester og forsvar, er konfidensialitet en forutsetning. Det gjør at vi noen ganger blir kritisert for hemmelighold og møtt med påstander om at vi gjør ting som vi faktisk ikke gjør. I teksten som følger svarer vi på spørsmål som vi ofte får. Vi setter stor pris på interessen for vårt selskap og vil gjerne bidra til at det som blir sagt og skrevet om oss og det vi gjør er korrekt. De som måtte lure på noe er velkomne til å ta kontakt via epostadresse media@palantir.com. Hva gjør egentlig Palantir? Vi utvikler og lisensierer programvare for datadrevne beslutnings- og arbeidsprosesser. Våre plattformer Palantir Gotham og Palantir Foundry kombinerer dataanalyse med spesifikke forretningsprosesser, og sørger for at de riktige dataene når de riktige brukerne og beslutningstakerne til rett tid. Dette muliggjør sofistikerte analyser, smidig samarbeid og kontinuerlige forbedringer av kundens virksomhet. For mer informasjon om Palantir Foundry og Palantir Gotham, besøk gjerne vår nettside. Er Palantir et dataselskap eller en dataminer? Palantir er et programvareselskap. I motsetning til mange teknologiselskaper er ikke forretningsmodellen vår basert på inntektsgenerering fra personlige data. I stedet utvikler og lisensierer vi programvare som muliggjør å integrere og analysere sine egne data fra forskjellige kilder for å ta bedre beslutninger. Databeskyttelse og sikkerhet er grunnleggende for Palantir og har fra begynnelsen av vært integrert i arkitekturen til programvaren. Men Palantir er ofte beskrevet som en dataforhandler eller datasamler. Bedriften har vel godt av tilgang til kundedata? Nei. Dette er en vanlig misforståelse som er lett å skjønne, fordi det er så mange andre aktører som gjør nettopp dette. Palantir skiller seg fra mengden ved at vi verken samler inn eller selger kundedata. Vi tillater heller ingen datautveksling mellom våre kunder, med mindre en slik utveksling er uttrykkelig etterspurt av kunder som samarbeider. Ethvert partnerskap med en kunde er fullstendig — kontraktsmessig, operasjonelt og teknologisk — atskilt fra alle andre kundeforhold. Vår programvare og tjenester brukes utelukkende etter instruks fra våre kunder: kunden, og bare kunden, bestemmer hvordan dataene skal brukes. Våre kunder har full kontroll over hvor og hvordan analyser utføres. Vi vil ikke, og kan ikke, gjenbruke eller overføre våre kunders data til våre egne formål. Å prøve å dra nytte av kundedata på denne måten ville blant annet undergravd tilliten som vi er avhengig av at våre kunder har til oss. Bruker Palantir kundedata til egne formål? Nei. Vi bruker heller ikke under noen omstendigheter AI-modeller som har blitt trent med kunders data, verken for våre egne formål eller for videresalg til tredjeparter. Brukte Palantir COVID-19-krisen for å få tilgang til konfidensielle helsedata? Nei. Palantir bruker ikke kundedata og gjør selvfølgelig ikke dette heller innenfor rammen av våre partnerskap i kampen mot COVID-19. I stedet er det våre kunder som bruker programvaren vår til å lovlig og hensiktsmessig vurdere sine egne data. Hvis det ikke handlet om tilgang til helsedata, hvorfor tilbød Palantir sine tjenester gratis under COVID-19-krisen? I noen tilfeller har Palantir tilbudt sin programvare pro bono i kampen mot COVID-19 fordi vi ønsker å bruke vår erfaring, ekspertise og programvare for å raskt kunne hjelpe til med en av de største globale utfordringene de siste tiårene. Palantirs rolle var å støtte en integrert og omfattende helsesystem-respons på pandemien. På denne måten var vi i stand til å sikre at beslutningstakerne til våre partnere har all relevant informasjon i kampen mot COVID-19 i omtrent sanntid. For tiden brukes vår programvare av det amerikanske departementet for helsetjenester (HHS) i sitt HHS Protect-program, og av National Health Service (NHS) i Storbritannia. Med HHS Protect er mer enn 150 forskjellige datakilder samlet i ett økosystem. Dette prosjektet integrerer data fra føderale, statlige og lokale myndigheter samt helseindustrien for å muliggjøre et helhetlig syn på hele helsesystemet. Vårt system gjør det mulig å samle og organisere slike data, og dataene forblir lagret hos de respektive eierne av data, uten at vi eller andre utenforstående har tilgang til dem. Det er mange programvareselskaper som tilbyr dataanalyse i en eller annen form. Hva skiller Palantir fra disse selskapene? Det er en rekke faktorer som gjør Palantir unikt og annerledes enn andre programvareselskaper. Vi ser på programvaren vår som et operativsystem for den moderne organisasjonen. Vi tilbyr en dataplattform, analysefunksjoner og økt kunnskap om virksomheten og operasjonelle prosesser. Vi er spesielt opptatte av å gjøre det mulig for kunder å ta bedre beslutninger som er baserte på omfattende og etterprøvbare data enten det er på samlebåndet eller i toppledelsen. Vi ser for oss at en organisasjon fungerer som summen av alle beslutningene den tar. Disse beslutningene er avhengige av hverandre og henger sammen på en kompleks måte. Det er ganske vanlig i de fleste organisasjoner at beslutninger tas i ulike avdelinger basert på ulike datasiloer og at kunnskapen om disse beslutningene forblir skjult for andre som kunne ha nytte av å vite. Palantirs plattformer skaper orden i datakaoset ved å gjøre det mulig for våre kunder å få en helhetlig oversikt over alle relevant data. Resultatet er en sammenkoblet organisasjon, og bedre og mer bærekraftige beslutninger. Vi drar nytte av vårt mangeårige arbeid med noen av de viktigste institusjonene i verden: Våre plattformer kan implementeres raskt og effektivt for kunder, og gir umiddelbare resultater. Basert på vår erfaring og teknologi kan vi redusere implementeringstiden fra måneder ned til dager. Som nevnt er databeskyttelse og datasikkerhet grunnleggende for Palantir og har vært integrert i programvarearkitekturen helt fra begynnelsen. Vårt mål er at våre plattformer ikke bare skal oppfylle gjeldende personvern- og databeskyttelsesregler. De skal også kontinuerlig utvikles i tråd med nye juridiske krav og anerkjente forventninger i samfunnet. Hvordan støtter Palantir sine kunder når det gjelder databeskyttelse? Våre langvarige kundeforhold inkluderer politi og etterretningstjenester, men også selskaper innen finans- og helsesektoren. Disse er alle institusjoner som jobber i svært sensitive og komplekse datamiljøer og som er underlagt strenge myndighetskrav. For å bistå disse organisasjonene i å oppfylle deres etiske og juridiske krav, har Palantir helt fra begynnelsen integrert og kontinuerlig videreutviklet relevante databeskyttelsesfunksjoner i programvarens arkitektur. Palantir-programvaren lar deg bestemme nøyaktig hvem som ser hvilke data og til hvilket formål, samtidig som man kan kontrollere nøyaktig hvor lenge data skal lagres. Fordi det opprettes detaljert historikk for integrasjon og transformasjon av hvert datapunkt, er det alltid mulig å spore når og hvordan dataene ble opprettet eller endret. Programvaren forenkler også rapportering mot ansvarlige tilsynsorganer. Vårt samarbeid med det danske rikspolitiet er et eksempel på hvordan våre produkter muliggjør streng databeskyttelse og ansvarlig håndtering av sensitiv informasjon. Det danske rikspolitiet bestemte seg for å samarbeide med Palantir fordi vi var den eneste programvare-leverandøren som var i stand til å oppfylle alle de strenge juridiske kravene til databeskyttelse. Ved hjelp av standardfunksjonalitet i Palantirs programvare er det mulig selv for ikke-tekniske brukere innen byrået å analysere aktivitet i plattformen og undersøke potensiell uredelighet. Det danske rikspolitiet beskrev implementeringen til den tyske ukeavisen Die Zeit som den viktigste anskaffelsen i dansk politis historie når det gjelder databeskyttelse. Palantir har jobbet med politi og etterretningstjenester i lang tid. Er Palantir et overvåkingsselskap? Nei. Palantir utvikler programvare som gjør det mulig for våre kunder å lovlig og effektivt behandle sine egne data. Vi driver ikke med overvåking eller spionasje, og vi selger ikke programvaren vår med det formål å muliggjøre overvåking som for eksempel kommunikasjonsovervåking. Palantir-produktene har unike egenskaper som er interessante for blant annet etterretning, men kunden er alltid nødt til å gjøre en juridisk vurdering av hva som er lovlig bruk av programvaren gitt sin myndighet og sitt formål. Palantir vil ikke tillate at programvaren blir brukt i strid med gjeldende lovgivning. Hva med rykter om at Palantir muliggjør prediktivt politiarbeid — er dette sant? Nei. Palantir tilbyr ikke et prediktivt politiverktøy. Palantir gir politistyrkene programvare som gjør dem i stand til å utføre sitt vanlige etterforskningsarbeid mer effektivt og i samsvar med gjeldende retningslinjer og prosedyrer. Hvorfor støtter Palantir GAIA-X-initiativet, som har som mål å styrke Europas digitale suverenitet? Palantirs medgründer og administrerende direktør, Dr. Alex Karp, har ofte uttrykt sin beundring for den sosiale markedsøkonomien i Europa og for den europeiske industriens tradisjon og enorme ekspertise. I motsetning til mange amerikanske teknologiselskaper ønsker ikke Palantir å konkurrere med eller endre de eksisterende forretningsmodellene til etablerte europeiske selskaper. Snarere ser vi på oss selv som partnere til disse selskapene og ønsker å følge dem på veien mot digital transformasjon. En sammenkoblet, åpen datainfrastruktur som den GAIA-X streber etter, vil være et stort skritt fremover her. Helt siden vi ble etablert tidlig på 2000-tallet har vi forholdt oss til spørsmål som også er relevante for GAIA-X: Hvordan kan institusjoner i offentlig og privat sektor vurdere distribuerte, heterogene datamengder som de har akkumulert gjennom flere tiår? Hvordan kan organisasjoner bruke data effektivt og samtidig samarbeide på tvers av organisasjonsgrenser uten å sette datasikkerhet og databeskyttelse i fare? Etter mer enn 17 års arbeid i svært komplekse, sterkt regulerte datamiljøer har vi utviklet en forståelse for hvordan teknologiske løsninger kan harmoniseres med retningslinjer for datastyring, lovbestemmelser og andre normative rammebetingelser. Det er nettopp denne erfaringen og kompetansen vi ønsker å bidra med i GAIA-X-prosjektet. Har Palantir noen gang vært involvert med Cambridge Analytica (CA) eller assosiert med forholdet mellom Facebook og CA? Nei. Det ble i sin tid hevdet i en nyhetsartikkel at så skulle være tilfelle, men det er ikke sant. Palantir har aldri hatt noe forretningsforhold med CA, verken kontraktsmessig eller på noen annen måte. Palantir har heller aldri jobbet med CA-data (inkludert data hentet fra Facebook). Palantir har vært oppsøkt av CA ved minst to anledninger (i 2013 og 2015), men har nektet å samarbeide på grunn av bekymringer rundt personvern og etikk, samt selskapets retningslinjer. Etter at en nyhetsartikkel antydet et samarbeid, gjennomførte vi en etterforskning som avslørte at en ansatt hadde et uavhengig forhold til CA uten Palantirs viten. Vedkommende ble sagt opp. Palantir jobber ikke med noen form for politiske kampanjer noe sted i verden. Hvordan muliggjør Palantir sikkert samarbeid mellom organisasjoner? Skywise er et godt eksempel på hvordan produktene våre muliggjør sikkert og kontrollert samarbeid innenfor organisasjoner og på tvers av organisasjonsgrenser. Dette er et digitalt økosystem for hele luftfartsindustrien levert av Airbus og basert på Palantir Foundry. Flyselskaper og leverandører innen luftfartsindustrien over hele verden bruker Skywise for å forbedre operasjonell effektivitet, sikkerhet og unngå forsinkelser. For eksempel kan leverandører optimalisere sine varelager og redusere sene leveranser. Airbus akselererer produksjon og utvikling av nye forretningsmodeller. Skywise bringer forskjellige, og til og med konkurrerende, organisasjoner sammen i et enkelt økosystem. Dette samarbeidet er muliggjort ved hjelp av en forent dataintegrasjonsarkitektur der deltakerne kan administrere sitt eget forente område og samarbeide for et bestemt formål og utveksle bestemte data på en sikker måte. Ville Palantir noen gang begrenset bruken av programvare av etiske årsaker? Ja. Palantir har gjort dette mange ganger. I en artikkel i Washington Post i september 2019, så vel som i mange andre intervjuer, har vår administrerende direktør Dr. Alex Karp erkjent selskapets etiske ansvar for å forhindre misbruk av teknologien. Palantir jobber kun med vestlige liberale demokratier og deres strategiske allierte. I alle tilfeller undersøker vi potensielle kunder og mulige bruksområder nøye for samsvar med våre verdier og prinsipper . For eksempel, som vi også tydeliggjorde i vår S-1-innlevering til det amerikanske kredittilsynet, SEC i 2020, driver ikke Palantir virksomhet med Kinas kommunistparti, er ikke vert for våre plattformer i Kina, og pålegger begrensninger på tilgang til plattformene våre i Kina. Vi vil heller ikke gjøre programvaren vår tilgjengelig for den russiske regjeringen. Palantir har takket nei til å samarbeide med mange andre internasjonale myndighetsorganer på grunn av bekymringer om menneskerettighetsbrudd. I mange år har Palantir hatt et dedikert team som tar seg av spørsmål om databeskyttelse og dataetikk. Mer informasjon om Palantirs tilnærming til Privacy and Civil Liberties Engineering finner du her.

title: Privacy & Civil Liberties Engineering (Palantir Explained, #5)
description: Editor’s note: This is the fifth post in Palantir Explained, a series that explores a range of topics, including our approach to privacy
author: Palantir
body: Privacy & Civil Liberties Engineering (Palantir Explained, #5) Editor’s note: This is the fifth post in Palantir Explained, a series that explores a range of topics, including our approach to privacy, security, AI/ML safety and more. Previous posts explored trust in data, our business model, purpose-based access controls, and data anonymization. Protecting privacy and upholding liberal democratic values have been central to Palantir’s identity and mission since our founding in 2003; and we have intentionally adopted a business model that allows us to follow through with this commitment. We make software that enables the institutions that serve our societies to use their data responsibly and effectively, and we do not trade in personal data at all. Many of the most important institutions in the world rely on Palantir software to support critical and sensitive operations. These organizations have exceptionally high security and data protection standards — for reasons ranging from protecting national security to complying with the world’s most stringent privacy laws — and they would not trust our software if it did not meet and exceed these standards. Achieving such a strong security record — and empowering institutions to protect people’s data in the process — was necessary for our business to succeed. For example, our earliest customers in national security required very fine-grained control over who could see what data, granting permissions only on a precise need-to-know basis. This functionality can equally enhance privacy when applied to other domains. We realized early on that effectively creating privacy-protective technology and business practices required a dedicated focus, a significant investment, and a broad mandate. This is why Palantir created one of the world’s first Privacy & Civil Liberties Engineering (“PCL”) teams more than a decade ago, which continues to be an essential part of the company’s identity and work. Rejecting Unacceptable Tradeoffs Poorly conceived technologies present false tradeoffs. One argument that we have long rejected is that national security requires sacrificing citizens’ privacy and civil liberties. Our experience has been that through the thoughtful and principled development of technology to support institutions, we can harmoniously advance these and other rights. It is essential, for example, to treat fairness as a first order concern when designing systems to support decision making. Ultimately, Palantir’s work is unjustifiable if it does not strengthen privacy and uphold liberal democratic values. Citizens would rightly oppose it, and we would be undermining the very societies and convictions that we seek to defend. Thus a motivating question for every engineer in the company is “Do I want to live in the kind of world that the technology we’re building would enable?” To help our engineers and leadership achieve this mission and navigate the difficult questions that arise, Palantir formed the Privacy & Civil Liberties Engineering (“PCL”) team as a specialist vanguard to advise and lead on these issues. The Privacy & Civil Liberties Engineering Team The goal of the PCL team is to design, build, and deploy privacy-protective technologies, and to foster a culture of responsibility around their development and use. The inclusion of the term “engineering” in this title is a deliberate one. Policy is essential, and our first obligation is always to follow policy as defined by public officials; but relying on policy alone to ensure ethical practice provides limited confidence that others can or will always adopt it. Similarly, compliance teams with a purely legalistic approach may fail to anticipate new issues that technological development presents. “Engineering” is a core responsibility of the PCL team in order to ensure that our values are encoded into our software at a fundamental level, and to ensure that the team is exposed to exactly the same issues as every other engineer in the company. This gives the PCL team a nuanced understanding of frontline issues, forcing us to be solution-oriented rather than being focused solely on academic theory with limited attachment to real-world tensions. As with policy and compliance, technical controls alone cannot avert negative societal outcomes, which are fundamentally human problems, and may arise in subtle, complex, and context-dependent ways. Navigating this interplay requires a diverse and multidisciplinary team, and so in addition to engineers, the team comprises lawyers, data scientists, policy specialists, social scientists, and philosophers, all of whom closely collaborate in the pursuit of holistic and thoughtful software development and deployment. We continually aspire to produce software according to the principle of “privacy by design and default.” This means that the standard configuration of the software is maximally privacy protective: any access that a user gets to personal data must be explicitly and deliberately permitted by the responsible organization; personal data should be deleted once its retention is no longer justified; data is displayed at the minimum necessary sensitivity; all user actions are auditable to ensure they act responsibly, and so forth. The team also contributes directly to product development, including developing “privacy-enhancing technologies” that can be deployed on top of default protections, supporting sophisticated encryption, justification, retention, and data-tracking approaches to meet a great range of compliance contexts and ethical imperatives. These tools enable our customers to meet — and often exceed — the most rigorous data handling standards; and we strive to give them the tools to set the bar for privacy expectations ever higher. Privacy Alone is Insufficient When making software for processing data, ethical engineering isn’t just about about privacy and data protection. Data is used as information about the world, often to make consequential decisions that will greatly affect people’s lives. The effects of these decisions vary across workflows and domains, as do the ethical concerns that must factor into them. While the PCL team works to foster a range of experience and expertise in order to respect key principles and to help our customers navigate these questions, ultimately the question of how data can be most responsibly used in all these contexts often requires us to engage directly with those who can supplement and enrich our perspectives. Thus, an essential second responsibility for the team is to act as interface between other subject-matter experts — from civil society, academic centers, or policymaking centers — and our engineers and customers. We continuously consult with these experts in order to ensure we are providing the most responsible, thoughtful, and effective guidance to our engineers and the organizations our products support. This means organizing lectures, discussions, and trainings within the company. It means meeting and consulting with a variety of community members and stakeholders — including those who may be critical of aspects of our work. It means participating in conferences, and ultimately being more transparent, including publishing blog posts, videos, and books about our work. We must keep working to set this transparency and engagement bar higher, and seek new ways of fulfilling this obligation. In 2012, we formed the Palantir Council of Advisors on Privacy & Civil Liberties (“PCAP”). These advisors are world-renowned experts representing a diversity of perspectives and deep expertise in legal practice, policy, technical, administrative, and other facets of the field. It includes a former Australia Privacy Commissioner, a founder of the prominent UK advocacy organization Big Brother Watch, a former US Department of Justice Chief Privacy Officer, an Engineering Chair in the Department of Informatics at Technische Universität München, a former White House Deputy Chief Technology Officer for Internet Policy, and a number of other foundational scholars and lawyers in the privacy legal field. All of this reflects a fundamental conviction of the company, strengthened by long experience: technology cannot solve all the world’s problems. The introduction of technologies into real world contexts can generate diverse and sometimes difficult-to-anticipate effects; responsible technological design must be infused with a respect for the complexity of this undertaking. To learn more about the work of the team, follow @PalantirPrivacy. Author Courtney Bowman, Global Director, Privacy & Civil Liberties Engineering, Palantir

title: Connected Utilities: The Path to a circular water economy
description: Water companies need to be bold and commit to being fully-integrated organisations
author: Palantir
body: Connected Utilities: The path to a circular water economy As the climate shifts, populations grow, and the standard of living expectations increase, clean water is an increasingly precious natural resource. The developed world takes clean running water for granted, and to sustain this, the industry must answer the ever-louder calls to achieve a circular economy. Minimising waste and raw inputs implies a finely optimised, closed-loop supply chain. This in turn requires a truly connected utility provider. Let’s look at the compelling reasons why the water industry would benefit from hyper-optimised operations and data integration. Net Zero is a data integration problem. And so is a fine-tuned supply chain. Ensuring that inputs and outputs are in harmony at every step of the closed-loop supply chain requires tracking flows at a granular scale. Granular detail enables granular decisions. Providing a high quality customer experience has never been more important. Historically, water utilities served properties. Today, they serve the modern consumer accustomed to hyper-customer-focused service. Great customer experience touches on everything from burst mains to accurate billing and nuanced education around sustainable consumption. Once again, progress requires a deeply connected approach. A circular supply chain demands a data operating system built for collaboration. In the current world, operations don’t map neatly to the water industry’s delivery targets (known in the UK sector as Outcome Delivery Incentives, or ODIs), which in turn don’t always map to budgets. The result is that collaboration is blocked, innovation is stifled and improvement potential falls through the cracks. The problem compounds when pursuing a circular supply chain. Digitisation can address the challenges of dealing with some of the world’s oldest civil infrastructure. Water utilities are responsible for operating critical subterranean infrastructure, which, in some cases (e.g., London’s sewer network) dates back to the 19th century. Building a digital twin of this infrastructure would enable visibility and empower collaboration across every aspect of the network. Successful data integration is a vital tool in the race to save the planet Achieving a circular economy in the water industry is the promised land of sustainability and achieving Net Zero targets. This approach would reduce pressure on finite and in-demand natural resources, as well as minimise and repurpose waste. Companies who can harness the power of connectivity will also be more empowered to meet their ODIs. Water utilities are responsible for complex engineering processes spread across vast swathes of the country. These processes range from: energy intensive (e.g. pumping), direct emitters (e.g. activated sludge processes emitting nitrous oxide), net positive (e.g. bio-methane to electricity) and finally, processes that could go either way like vehicle fleets (e.g Electric Vehicles). Net Zero is a data integration problem — meaningful decisions are those that are made on top of a granular digital twin of a water company’s enterprise. They are made with full view of the trade-offs and the downstream impacts, and with carbon intensity accounted for at the atomic level of activity. A connected water utility uses its digital twin to investigate trade-offs and simulate what-if scenarios. This is a particularly powerful tool used in risk evaluation, for example in assessing, mitigating and preparing for service disruption during severe weather. Driving customer experience within a connected company From a consumer perspective, people expect water suppliers to provide them with clean water, manage, repurpose and minimise waste, and provide exceptional customer service. Compared to other household costs, we are generally less conscious of water on a use-by-use basis. We turn on the tap and it flows freely, almost always. For water utilities, this can mean that customer interactions are minimal, but frequently negative. Consumers typically only make contact when something is wrong. This is a significant challenge for water companies who must prioritise positive customer feedback or risk regulatory penalisation. The solution requires water providers to pursue a connected utility vision. Ideally, customer-focused decisions would be analysis-driven, referencing all of the relevant data, and decisions themselves are valued for the data points they represent. A connected utility could rapidly notify customers about potential supply interruptions, whilst having all of the necessary information instantly at hand to drive a resolution. Contact centre staff and operators share a common source of truth presented in holistic, flexible apps that reflect their world, not the underlying IT. Collaboration is key Building a connected utility requires that data is accessible to operational users across the business in a framework that reflects their world. It goes without saying that unfettered access to all data is not the answer. Collaboration (within an organisation and between organisations) is built on trust and security — granular security that reflects the purpose of the data usage. A connected water utility which achieves the circular ambition will harness huge volumes of data. This data will describe in near-realtime the entire asset base from reservoir to meter and from sewer to treatment plant. They will also describe–crucially–the customer that sits in the centre and their relationship to the assets and asset events. Success means wrangling legacy systems and harmonising them with modern ERP and CRMs within a single operating system that drives data-driven decision making. Digital Rome won’t be built in a day Digitalising asset data in pursuit of a digital twin is a challenge for modern assets that reside above the earth’s surface, let alone for the vast networks of pipes and sewers underground. With subterranean assets, the challenges can be as fundamental as understanding if the asset is where we think it is. What this amounts to is a data quality problem (on a potentially huge scale), and what it calls for is software which empowers operators and technicians in the field to feed their observations securely back in to the digital twin, improving it as they go. This software should be seamless parsing these suggested improvements and writing back validated adjustments to vital operational systems. In order to reach the goal of a circular economy, water companies need to be bold and commit to being fully-integrated organisations, one where operational silos are torn down and replaced with optimised operations. Palantir Foundry enables impactful collaboration, empowering our customers to integrate data sources and make informed decisions using a powerful digital twin. If you think your operations could benefit from data-powered decision making with Foundry, check out our Utilities offering. Or if you’d like to talk to some existing Foundry customers or a few of our engineers, just get in touch. Author Dr. Ben Hall, Deployment Strategist, Palantir UK

title: Finding a Growth Path at Palantir
description: The people and the mentorship are what Khanh Vu values most about working at Palantir.
author: Palantir
body: Finding a Growth Path at Palantir Test drive I looked out the window: it was an uncharacteristically cloudy day in Southern California. I had just gotten off a call with my team lead. My one-year anniversary at Palantir was around the corner, and with it came the recognition that I was no longer a new hire fresh out of college. I was now expected to own parts of the codebase, lead my own meetings, and answer all types of questions, technical and non-technical. People thought that with one year of exposure to this company and to this industry, I should be able to form my own opinions by now. The conversation I had just had with my lead seemed a repetition of so many smaller conversations with other coworkers: “Where do you see your career in five years?” I unconsciously shook my head. Where did everyone get this number — five years? What was it about this arbitrary mark of time that was so important? I had graduated from college a year ago. In five years’ time, I would be twenty-seven. I joined Palantir during the COVID-19 pandemic, when everything was in flux and life itself was uncertain. I thought I was only giving this role, this industry, and most of all, this company, a test drive of a year or so. I sat through onboarding sessions, listening wide-eyed to other twenty-two-year-olds talk about how they want to make contributions to Palantir’s renowned technology, how they hope to change the way Palantir operates as a company, or how they aspire to use that technology to change the world from the frontline of wars and pandemics. How could these people, who were the same age as I was, know with such certainty their passions and goals? It seemed that everyone around me, regardless of tenure, had already figured out why they were at Palantir, and where exactly in their career they were. It’s alright, I told myself. It wasn’t like I planned on staying at this company for long anyway, right? Definition of a “dev” Just after hitting the one-year marker, I moved to New York, out of my parents’ house, where I had stayed through the first year of my job. I started to go in-person to Palantir’s New York office. I sat with other people from my organization, called Production Infrastructure (PI), and began to learn everyone’s names, along with their favorite office snacks. We would grab lunch and dinner together every day, and do the weekly New York Times crossword puzzle on Friday afternoons. Everyone was so welcoming — I only want to contribute to make it even more so. I began organizing my own social activities for PI in New York, from group dinners to Secret Santa to the PI holiday party, even trips to Home Depot to get office plants for our desks. “Should we nominate Khanh to be our PI social chair from now on then?” someone said, as we were waiting for the elevator, holding our office plants. I grinned — if there was such a position, I would have loved to fill it. Everyone was so welcoming — I only want to contribute to make it even more so. Around the same time I moved to New York, the Class of 2021 joined the company, and my team took on a new grad hire, with whom I was given the same project in the fall of 2021. He was a backend engineer who was interested in systems architecture — he wanted to build clean and logical APIs. He worked hard, never afraid to face problems he didn’t understand head-on, and always ready to expand his knowledge, regardless of the effort and time he would have to put in. It was easy to see that he was motivated by the technical challenges he solved, and that he wanted to grow into a good systems engineer, to write great architectural proposals. He was only three months into Palantir, but already he was responsible for the backend of an entire project. I thought back to when I was three months into my job at Palantir. Did I have as much confidence in my role at the time? I couldn’t help but feel that I was not growing fast enough, in this company where everyone was so self-driven. What if I was not good enough, and newer hires would come to replace me? I brought this up with my lead at one point, thinking he would tell me to work harder, to become more efficient. Instead, he smiled at me and said, “There’s always more than enough room for both of you to grow together.” I had never even paused to ponder whether this was true. Tech recruiting out of college was so cutthroat: it made me believe there was no alternative to this zero-sum game. But there was never just one definition of what a “dev” should be at Palantir — there was so much space and flexibility for us both to grow. Day-to-day Once, on another occasion when I was discussing potential next projects with my lead, we quickly realized that the type of project I should take on depended on what I wanted to grow into. Unfortunately, I was missing that side of the equation. “It’s clear to see what some other new hires’ growth paths would be, whether they want to become an independent contributor, a people lead, or a tech lead. But your growth path is a little less clear to me, Khanh,” my lead said to me. He said it gently, more like a question to both of us than a comment, and I couldn’t help but smile. Has my lead truly put this much thought into my growth? During their weekly one-on-one meetings with me, my mentor and lead constantly checked in on whether I still liked the projects I was doing. My answer was always yes — I thought that was because I didn’t care enough about my work, but only later on did I realize it was rather because of the extraordinary amount of effort and thoughtfulness my lead and mentor had put into choosing projects for me. It’s this level of thoughtfulness and support that make me love coming into work every day. Yes, I enjoy the technical aspects of my job as well: I am never bored, the tasks are more than challenging enough to keep me engaged. I am trusted and given ownership and full reign for creativity. But, for me, it was never about the technical problems I get to solve as much as it was about the mentorship I received and the friendships I made along the way. I love waking up every morning to come into work, to say hi to those who sit near me, to grab coffee with people outside my organization, to walk around the office and see friendly, familiar faces — and, most importantly, to know that I work with people who care about my well-being. But, for me, it was never about the technical problems I get to solve as much as it was about the mentorship I received and the friendships I made along the way. That, to me, is the most important thing about work: being happy with your job. And I’ve come to realize that a job that makes you happy cannot just consist of the technical problems you would solve — it must also include the people, the culture, the atmosphere. All these things add up to your entire experience, and if their combination does not make you happy, then no amount of intellectual challenge will. Growth On occasion, I am asked to get on the phone with candidates currently interviewing with Palantir to answer questions about company culture and work/life balance. This is an extremely challenging task, because I do not know how to sound genuine when I say: “People at Palantir truly care about me, not only as a coworker but also as a person.” I would hear the candidate on the other end of the line chuckle nervously, probably thinking the recruiter was paying me to tell them this. If only I could tell them how I am now looking back at what I thought would be my one and only year at Palantir, how I’m laughing at the thought that this was just a “test drive”, how it has now been a year and a half and I have no intention of leaving. I wish I could also tell them that starting their first job out of college, they do not need to have a firm idea for where they are now or where they want to be in five years. Their job, their career, and their teammates should give them enough space to figure that out. That’s what real growth should look like. I wish I could also tell them that starting their first job out of college, they do not need to have a firm idea for where they are now or where they want to be in five years. I want to tell them that Palantir is special, because we allow for that space for growth: that undefined, more well-rounded career path that many other companies do not provide. There are enough recruiting emails and blog posts out there to tell them why they should join Palantir for the technical challenges that they will solve here and for the real-world impact they get to make on the job. But I want to tell them why they should join for reasons other than that — the mentorship, the culture, the space for creativity, the flexibility for growth, and, most important of all, the people. But despite all these things, I don’t. I don’t tell them any of this on the phone, smiling a little at their nervous chuckles, because they did not ask. Besides, how could one sound sincere about how great their company was on the phone? So instead I only say, “Why yes, we do have an espresso machine in the office. We also have a freezer full of ice cream. Can I entice you with that?” Khanh Vu joined Palantir in September 2020 as a new grad hire. She is currently a frontend engineer on the Apollo Platform product.

title: Palantir Developers: Learn to build in Palantir Foundry
description: Introducing new resources for developers to elevate their impact in Foundry.
author: Palantir
body: Palantir Developers: Learn to build in Palantir Foundry Introducing New Resources for Developers to Elevate their Impact in Foundry Everyone in an organization should be able to use the right data to make the best decisions. That’s why Palantir is committed to making Foundry as intuitive and accessible as possible — not only for data scientists and engineers, but also for sales, product development, recruiting, and more. We believe the best way to accelerate towards this vision is to empower the thousands of developers that build on Foundry every day. To make this happen, we’re starting to engage more with developers on Stack Overflow and are launching a new video channel created for the developer community. Answering Your Developer Questions For years, we’ve provided our customers’ developers with product documentation within Foundry, and collaborated together live on the front lines. But as COVID changed the way we work, developers and Palantirians needed to find new ways to collaborate. Recently, we’ve seen these developers searching the internet with questions about Foundry, whether learning how to debug data pipelines, or seeking ideas on implementation design. Over time, we’ve seen Stack Overflow steadily become a place where they could find answers. We’re excited to make developer engagement on Stack Overflow a core part of our work. Developer thoughts, questions, and collaborations are welcome here. Palantir Developers Video Channel We are also excited to launch the Palantir Developers channel, marking a new phase of developer support across our customer base. If images are worth a thousand words, then videos are a library. The channel will serve as a hub to help developers unlock even more value within Foundry. Check out our new channel and subscribe here: Palantir Developers Channel From tutorials about writing unit tests to walkthroughs of a Foundry Reference Project, the Palantir Developers channel will feature multiple video series highlighting different developer topics on Foundry. Our customers’ developers use Foundry in innovative ways we never could have imagined when we first released it six years ago. They play a critical role in shaping our products. We’ve embedded deeply with developers to build new features and even new tools. Together, we’ve created new charts and filters, simplified app building with Workshop, and designed Quiver to help developers overlay millions of sensor data points in seconds. We are optimistic that this channel will provide developers a collaborative space to learn, share, and be inspired to build new solutions.

title: Palantir Japanで働く — 広範なインパクトを生み出す、意義ある仕事
description: Working at Palantir Japan: Broad Impact, Meaningful Purpose
author: Palantir
body: Palantir Japanで働くーここには、大きなインパクトを生み出す理由がある。 パランティア テクノロジーズ ジャパン (Scroll down for English translation below) 日本には、歴史的基盤とグローバルな影響力を併せ持つ強力な企業が集まっています。これらの企業が業界を引っ張る競争力を保つには、最先端のソフトウェアが必要です。私たちPalantir Japanは、高齢化社会におけるヘルスケア の成果向上から、急成長するスタートアップ企業のための規模の拡大が容易なツール、日本最大級の製造拠点 における効率改善に至るまで、パートナー企業とともに意義あるインパクトの創出に取り組んでいます。 インパクトを生み出す Palantirは世界中で最も困難な課題の解決に取り組んでおり、Palantir Japanでの取り組みはまだ始まったばかりです。どこの拠点であっても、どのチームに所属していても、あなたは、ミッションの遂行を左右する問題へのソリューションを共に構築する集団の、そして最善のアイデアに価値を見出す会社の一員です。インパクトを生み出す仕事をしたい方は、ぜひ応募をご検討ください。 Forward Deployed Software Engineer (Delta) Deployment Strategist (Echo) 上記の二つの職種は、募集中の多くの職種の一部に過ぎません。その他の職種や最新の募集状況については、キャリアページをご覧ください。どの職種が自分に向いているかわからなくても大丈夫です。当社の採用チームがあなたに最適な職種を見つけるお手伝いをいたします。 Palantirの日本における仕事は、才能ある社員たちがいて初めて可能になります。Palantirの製品を構築する、驚くべき才能を持った社員たちは私たちの誇りです。このブログでは、Palantir Japanの社員たちに、彼らがPalantirに入社した経緯と、彼らが取り組んでいる意義ある仕事について聞きました。 Palantirに入社した理由を教えてください。 Jiali C (Echo) 東京で開かれたキャリアフォーラムで初めてPalantirのことを知ったのですが、その時に実際に働いている社員に会い、製品についてよりくわしく聞くことができました。Palantirとの面接では、履歴書の経歴ではなく、私がどんな人間で、成長のポテンシャルを持っているかどうかということを見られている、と心から思いました。また、日本の伝統的な企業に比べて、Palantirはより先進的でペースの速い仕事文化であるところがとても良いと思いました。 Sho H (Echo) Palantirの製品にとても興味を惹かれました。実は前職ではPalantirのカスタマだったのですが、日本企業や世界中の企業が抱える最も困難な課題を解決できるプラットフォームだと思いました。当時のやり取りの中で、Palantirのチームや文化にも非常に強い感銘を受けました。私がやり取りをしたPalantir社員は皆仕事が速く、賢く、協力的で、他の会社とは非常に異なっていました。Palantirに入社すれば、きっと我が家にいるように感じるだろうと思いました。 Henry T (Delta) Palantirは、多くの日本企業よりもかなり速いペースで事業を進めます。自分が興味を惹かれたプロジェクトを担当できる自由度も、より高いです。技術面の話をすれば、バックエンドの開発からフロントエンドまで、またETLからフロントエンドのアプリケーションまで、様々なテクノロジーに網羅的に関われることにも興味を惹かれました。技術以外の面では、幅広い業界にまたがる具体的な課題を解決できる製品の仕事であることがとても良いと感じました。Palantirはまた、非常に野心的な目標を持つ多様なカスタマ基盤を有し、その野心的な目標のスケールの大きさと、プロジェクトの重要性が、この仕事をとても刺激的なものにしてくれています。 Katsushige K (Echo) より多くの日本企業が、ゆっくりとではありますが、DXを進めてきているトレンドを目の当たりにしてきました。多くの企業にとって、古くなったデータインフラを最新のものに更新するプロセスは非常に重要であり、私もその進化に関わりたいと思いました。Palantirに入社後は、多くの異なる業界を担当し、彼らのテクノロジーの最新化を手伝う機会に恵まれています。 Palantir Japanにおけるあなたの職務について聞かせてください。 Henry T (Delta) Forward Deployed Software Engineer、またはDeltaと呼ばれる職種で、カスタマーと直接やり取りをしてニーズを理解し、そのニーズを満たすためのソリューションをFoundryの中に構築する機会に恵まれています。当社の中核となる製品を構築するだけでなく、それがどのようにカスタマーの役に立つのかを直接見られるのは、この職種ならではだと思います。私たちが構築する製品と、それが生み出すインパクトの間に垣根はありません — プロセス全体の最初から最後までに関わることができています。 Kenta D (Echo) Deployment Strategist、またはEchoと呼ばれる職種で、当社のソフトウェアによって、ユーザーがデータに基づいたより良い意思決定を行えるようにするのが私の役目です。カスタマーに最大の価値をもたらすために、どこでどのようにデータを活用できるかを見極めようとする中で、カスタマーの組織内の多種多様なステークホルダーがよく見えてくるようになります。カスタマーのデータが秘める可能性を解き放つ、という全体的な課題は不変である一方、複数の業界にまたがったカスタマーを担当しているため、毎日新しいことに出会えます。 Sho H (Echo) Deployment Strategistとしての職務の中で最もやりがいを感じることの一つは、カスタマーが真に求めていることをカスタマー自身が理解する手助けができることです。データを活用する上での課題についてカスタマーが話すのをよく耳にしますが、事業のオペレーションを改善するためにどのようにデータを使うべきなのかをカスタマーだけで考えるのは難しい場合もあります。Foundryをそのようなカスタマーに紹介し、多様な目的に使えるFoundryの能力を理解してもらう手助けをしつつ、私自身もFoundryの機能を最大限に活用する方法を学ぶことで、パートナーを組む企業・団体が驚くような成果を出すのを目の当たりにしてきました。 Palantir Japanオフィスの職場環境について教えてください。 Henry T (Delta) Palantir Japanチームは全員がとても協力的で、互いにサポートし合っています。チームはまだ拡大中の段階であることから、それぞれが担当する多くのプロジェクトについてお互いに助け合う気持ちを皆が持っていて、親密なコミュニティになっています。一方で大規模なグローバル企業の一部でもあることから、日本のオフィスを構成するリソースや、カスタマーに最高のソリューションを提供するために必要なリソースはすべて提供されています。 Sho H (Echo) 今まで働いた会社に比べて、はるかに融通の利く環境です。通常は、自分の生産性を最も高められる時間を自由に選んで出社や退社ができます。チームメンバーに直接会って質問したり、一緒に仕事を進めたりできるので、オフィスに来るのは楽しみです。また、オフィスが原宿にあり、周囲においしいものが食べられる場所がたくさんあるところも良いです。 Katsuhige K (Echo) 昨今ますます拡大している日本企業のDXの取り組みに直接関われることにとてもわくわくしています。この仕事は今後日本中でより普遍的に求められるものになっていきますし、日本を最先端の国にする鍵となる役目をこれから果たしていく成長中の東京オフィスの初期メンバーであることに誇りを感じています。 Makoto S (Sales) フレンドリーで協力的なチームのことは、もうすでに他のメンバーたちが話していることと思います。加えてお話ししたいのは、事前予約なしにさっと打ち合わせができる場所を多く備えたきれいなオフィスに、世界で最も困難な課題を解決することに情熱を傾けている同僚たちがたくさんいることです。オフィスにいるだけでその情熱を感じられ、まさにそれがベストの仕事をするための環境を作り出しています。 あなたにとってPalantirにおける成長とは？ Makoto S (Sales) Palantirは世界的にも成長していますが、Palantir Japanは特に成長の初期段階にある会社のように感じます。このような驚くべき仕事をしている会社で最初期の段階から働けていることにワクワクしています。Palantirは数年後には日本中の企業に最も価値あるソリューションのいくつかを提供し、日本の産業と社会全体に影響を与えるようになるだろうと心から思っています。そのような過程の中で役割を果たすことは、自身のスキルを築き、この会社を成功させるため個人として大きな責任を果たす機会がたくさんあるということです。 Kenta D (Echo) 非常に重要な課題の解決に取り組んでいるため、日々の仕事の中で多くの難しい問題や困難に直面します。同時に、そのような困難が、一人ひとり異なる形での成長を加速させます。とはいえ、私は非常に優秀で有能な、そして協力的な同僚たちに囲まれています。また、頻繁にメンターやリーダーと話し合って、自分の方向性が間違っていないか確認しています。はっきりと言えるのは、そのような困難の中でも自分が独りぼっちだと感じたことは一度もないということです。 Jiali C (Echo) Palantirでは、絶えず変化するカスタマーのニーズと、それに応える製品を扱っているため、日々成長の機会があります。ペースの速い環境と、多様な課題を通じて、ステークホルダーとの調整とタスク管理について多くを学びました。本当に成功するためには、プロジェクトマネジメントや熟考、技術的スキルやその他多くのことを学ぶ必要があります。さらに重要なこととして、非常に多くの異なる業界やカスタマーを担当する中で、解決策を見つけ出すためにどのようにして常に問題の深掘りを行えば良いのかを学びました。 仕事に応募する Forward Deployed Software Engineer (Delta) Deployment Strategist (Echo) Working at Palantir Japan: Broad Impact, Meaningful Purpose Palantir Technologies Japan Japan is home to industrial powerhouse companies with historic foundations and global reach. To maintain their leading edge, these companies require cutting edge software. At Palantir Japan, we work with our partners to deliver meaningful impact, from improving healthcare outcomes for an aging population, to equipping rapid growth startups with scalable tools, to enabling heightened efficiencies in some of Japan’s largest manufacturing hubs. Make a Difference We work throughout the world to solve the most complex problems, and at Palantir Japan we’re just getting started. No matter where you’re based or which team you work on, you’ll be part of a group of people working together to build solutions to mission-critical problems and a company that values the very best ideas. If you’d like to make a difference, consider joining us: Forward Deployed Software Engineer (Delta) Deployment Strategist (Echo) These are just two roles of many others we are hiring for. Check out our Careers page for the latest openings and additional roles. Not sure about which role is best for you? Our Recruiting team can help you find your best fit. Palantir’s work in Japan is possible because of the talented people we employ, and we are proud to have incredible talent that make building out Palantir’s products possible. In this blog, we hear from members of Palantir Japan about their path to Palantir and the meaningful work that they do. Why did you join Palantir? Jiali C (Echo) When I first came across Palantir at a career forum held in Tokyo, I had the chance to meet current employees and hear more about the products. During my discussions with Palantir I felt truly considered for who I was and my potential for growth instead of who I was on paper. I also loved the fact Palantir had a fast paced progressive work culture compared to some traditional companies in Japan! Sho H (Echo) Palantir’s product really caught my eye. I was actually a customer of Palantir in a prior role, and believed the platform could solve the most difficult problems for organizations in Japan and around the world. My experience with the team and culture at Palantir also left a really strong impression. How we worked with them was very different from other companies — everyone I spoke to was very quick, smart, and cooperative. I knew joining Palantir, I’d feel right at home. Henry T (Delta) Palantir operates much more nimbly than many other companies in Japan. I have more freedom to own projects that grab my interest. From the technical side, I was also interested in having exposure to the whole tech stack — from backend development to frontend, from ETL to frontend applications. From the nontechnical side, I loved the idea of working on a product that can solve such specific problems across a broad range of industries. We also have a diverse customer base who are all really ambitious, and the scale of ambition and critical nature of projects make the work incredibly exciting. Katsushige K (Echo) I’ve watched the growing trend of Japanese companies slowly undergoing their digital transformation. It’s an incredibly important process for many businesses to modernize their aging data infrastructure, and I wanted to be a part of this evolution. At Palantir I have the opportunity to touch many different industries and help bring their tech into the modern age! What is your role at Palantir Japan? Henry T (Delta) As a Forward Deployed Software Engineer, or Delta, I have the opportunity to directly engage with our customers to understand their needs and build out solutions to address them in Foundry. The role is unique as it involves not only building out our core product but also seeing face to face how it helps our customers. There are no barriers between what you’re building and the impact it makes — I get to be a part of the whole process from end to end. Kenta D (Echo) As a Deployment Strategist, or Echo, my role is ensuring our software is helping our users make better, data-driven decisions. This gives me a lot of visibility into a variety of stakeholders throughout our customer’s organization, as I work to understand where and how we can leverage data to provide the maximum value to our customers. Though the broader challenge of unlocking the potential of our customer’s data is consistent, I’m working with customers across a number of industries making every day unique! Sho H (Echo) One of the most rewarding parts of my role as a Deployment Strategist is helping customers understand what they really want. I often hear customers describe their pain points working with data, and it can be challenging for them to imagine how to use data to make operational improvements to their business. By introducing them to Foundry, helping them understand its versatile capabilities, and learning myself how best we can leverage them, I’ve seen incredible results at the organizations we partner with. What’s it like to work at the Japan office? Henry T (Delta) Everyone in the Palantir Japan team has been incredibly collaborative and supportive. The team is still growing which has made a tight knit community of people all willing to help out with the many projects you’re working on. Yet we’re also a part of a larger global organization, which comes with all the resources we could need to build our local office and provide the best solutions to our customers. Sho H (Echo) There’s definitely a lot more flexibility than I’m used to. You can usually come and go from the office whenever makes most sense for you to be productive. I do enjoy coming to the office so I can ask questions and collaborate with team members in person. It also helps the office is in Harajuku, with a lot of great food options nearby! Katsuhige K (Echo) I’m really excited to be involved directly in digital transformation activities at Japanese companies, which has been a growing trend recently. The task will only become a more common need for businesses throughout the country, and being an early part of the growing Tokyo office that will be a key part of modernizing Japan is a great honor! Makoto S (Sales) I’m sure everyone has already shared about our friendly and collaborative team. I want to add that the office is a beautiful physical space with a lot of space for impromptu collaboration, filled with colleagues that are passionate about solving the world’s toughest problems. I can really feel that passion just being in the office and it really nurtures an environment to put our best work out. What does growth at Palantir look like for you? Makoto S (Sales) Though Palantir is growing globally, Palantir Japan especially feels like an early growth-stage company. It’s exciting being in this early on the ground floor for a company that does such incredible work. I honestly do think in a few years, Palantir will be providing some of the most valuable software solutions for companies around Japan, making impact for both businesses and broader society. Being a part of that journey means so much opportunity to build on my skills and have a big personal responsibility in helping this company succeed. Kenta D (Echo) Because of the critical problems we are solving, we face many tough questions and challenges in our day-to-day work. At the same time, these challenges really fuel our growth, which looks different for everyone. That said, I’m surrounded by incredibly smart, capable, and supportive colleagues. I also have frequent discussions with my mentors and leads to ensure I’m on the right track. What I can say with certainty is that I’ve never felt isolated in these challenges. Jiali C (Echo) At Palantir, we have the opportunity to grow on a daily basis as we work with constantly evolving customer needs and a product that answers those needs. The fast-paced environment and diversity of challenges has definitely taught me a lot on managing stakeholders and keeping track of my work. To really succeed you need to learn project management, reflection, technical skills, and more. More importantly, the exposure to so many different industries and customers has taught me how to always dig deeper on problems to seek solutions. title: Palantir und Digitale Souveränität
description: Bewahrung der Handlungsfähigkeit in einer Welt in Bewegung
author: Palantir
body: Palantir und Digitale Souveränität Bewahrung der Handlungsfähigkeit in einer Welt in Bewegung (Scroll down for English translation below) Daten sind der Treibstoff unserer heutigen Gesellschaft. Von der Gewährleistung der Grundversorgung bis hin zur Führung eines erfolgreichen Unternehmens, unser privater wie beruflicher Alltag wird zunehmend von der Fähigkeit bestimmt, Daten in großem Umfang verarbeiten zu können. Das Leben in einer digitalisierten Welt schafft lebensverbessernde Möglichkeiten für Innovation. Es bedeutet aber auch, dass Fortschritt zunehmend eine schnelle und effektive Verarbeitung von Daten und einen verantwortungsvollen Umgang mit diesen bedingt. Palantir stellt sich dieser Verantwortung. Unsere Kunden verarbeiten ihre Daten in unseren Plattformen, um den wichtigsten Herausforderungen unserer Zeit zu begegnen: von der Reform des Gesundheitswesens und dem Kampf gegen die globale Hungerkrise bis zur Gestaltung der Zukunft der Mobilität. Viele dieser Herausforderungen verlangen von unseren Kunden Einsatzfähigkeit und Belastbarkeit in Zeiten fundamentaler Unsicherheit und Unruhen. Oft bewegen sie sich auch in einem Umfeld, in dem die Grenzen zwischen freier Wirtschaft und hoheitlichen Aufgaben verschwimmen. Als Softwareunternehmen sind wir also mit der dringenden und berechtigten Frage konfrontiert, wie wir die Nutzung unserer Plattformen zur Verarbeitung von Daten einerseits, aber auch die Wahrung der Kontrolle und Verfügungsgewalt unserer Kunden über ihre Daten andererseits, ermöglichen können. In diesem Blogpost erklären wir Palantirs Verständnis von digitaler Souveränität und warum die Gewährleistung digitaler Souveränität eine so bedeutende Rolle in unserer Softwareentwicklung spielt. Besonders hervorheben möchten wir dabei die Investitionen, die wir schon heute tätigen, um unseren Kunden dabei zu helfen, den regulatorischen und geopolitischen Anforderungen von morgen zu begegnen. Digitale Souveränität Digitale Souveränität hat sowohl eine sicherheitspolitische als auch eine wirtschaftliche Komponente. Doch obwohl der Begriff geläufig geworden ist, bleibt die Bedeutung digitaler Souveränität nach wie vor umstritten. Auf der einen Seite der Debatte dominiert der Protektionismus, d.h. die Vorstellung, dass nur in heimischen Märkten gebaute Technologien zur Verarbeitung staatlich und wirtschaftspolitisch relevanter Daten genutzt werden sollen. In diesem Fall wird digitale Souveränität gleichgestellt mit Autarkie. Doch in Anbetracht der Geschwindigkeit gesellschaftlichen und wirtschaftlichen Fortschritts heutzutage erscheint die Vorstellung, sich ausschließlich auf in heimischen Märkten gebaute Technologien zu beschränken, illusorisch. Ob digital oder nicht, fast jede innovative Technologie schöpft Inspiration oder besteht aus international entwickelten Bestandteilen. Der beeindruckend schnelle Fortschritt in der Entwicklung von Impfstoffen im Kampf gegen die COVID-19 Pandemie hat die Vorzüge internationaler Zusammenarbeit noch einmal klar hervorgehoben. Sich dem enormen Potenzial zu verschließen, auf bereits bestehende Innovationen weiter aufzubauen, wäre daher nicht nur ein Fehler. In Anbetracht der dringenden Herausforderungen, mit denen wir als Gesellschaft heute konfrontiert sind, wäre dies auch eine verantwortungslose Verschwendung knapp bemessener Zeit. Souveränität bedeutet letztlich Handlungsfähigkeit, und diese bedingt zunehmend die Fähigkeit, Daten in großem Umfang zu analysieren und die auf dieser Basis getroffenen Entscheidungen in die Praxis umzusetzen. Gleichzeitig müssen Organisationen, um in einer zunehmend digital bestimmten Welt autonom zu agieren, zu jeder Zeit volle Kontrolle über ihre Daten und Entscheidungsfindung haben. Für Palantir bedeutet digitale Souveränität daher die Fähigkeit sowohl öffentlicher als auch privater Institutionen, die beste schon heute verfügbare Technologie zur Verarbeitung ihrer Daten zu nutzen, um auch noch morgen wettbewerbsfähig zu sein — zugleich aber die volle Kontrolle über ihre Daten und Entscheidungen zu behalten. Autonom Agieren Unsere Kunden dabei zu unterstützen, mithilfe unserer Technologien autonom zu agieren, stand schon immer im Mittelpunkt unserer Softwareentwicklung. Die Integration und Analyse von Daten in unseren Plattformen sind für uns kein Selbstzweck. Stattdessen ermöglichen sie es unseren Kunden, aus Daten schneller Erkenntnisse zu gewinnen und diese in die Lösung konkreter Probleme zu übersetzen. Die Entscheidungsfindung unserer Kunden zu erleichtern und es ihnen so zu ermöglichen, ihre Handlungsfähigkeit radikal zu beschleunigen, ist der Kern unseres Geschäftsmodells und unseres Erfolgs. Vor allem aber ist Palantir eine Softwarefirma, keine Datenfirma. Wir sammeln, analysieren oder verkaufen Kundendaten nicht für eigene Zwecke, noch sind wir in der Entscheidungsfindung unserer Kunden involviert. Unser Ziel ist es, unseren Kunden das Betriebssystem für nachhaltigen Erfolg zu liefern. Dahingehend bieten wir unseren Kunden Plattformen, mit denen sie ihre eigenen Daten im Einklang mit ihren eigenen Regeln und Zielen verarbeiten können. Von Beginn an eingebaute Funktionalitäten zur Gewährleistung des Datenschutzes und der Datensicherheit ermöglichen es ihnen dabei nicht nur darauf zu vertrauen, sondern sich auch immer wieder selbst zu vergewissern, dass ihre Daten sicher, integer und verlässlich verfügbar sind. Eine Welt im Wandel Von Brexit bis Schrems II sind unsere Kunden mit dem konstanten Risiko plötzlicher Umbrüche konfrontiert. Eine zunehmend fragmentierte politische und regulatorische Landschaft gefährdet ihre Handlungsfähigkeit. Doch je unsicherer unsere Welt wird auf globaler Ebene, desto wichtiger wird es für unsere Kunden, die Kontrolle über ihre Daten zu behalten und zwar dort, wo sie sind. Deswegen haben wir uns auch verpflichtet, es unseren Kunden zu ermöglichen, ihre Daten ausschließlich innerhalb ihrer jeweils eigenen Grenzen zu verarbeiten — nicht nur in den USA, sondern auch im Vereinigten Königreich und in der EU. Dies ist für uns eine beträchtliche technische und finanzielle Investition. Doch sie ist es uns wert, denn damit geben wir unseren Kunden etwas, was unbezahlbar ist: nämlich die Zuversicht, dass sie in der Zusammenarbeit mit uns zu jeder Zeit volle Kontrolle über ihre Daten und Entscheidungsfindung haben. Somit wahren sie ihre Handlungsfähigkeit — unabhängig von jeglichen politischen, regulatorischen und technischen Disruptionen. Palantir and Digital Sovereignty: Preserving Autonomy in an Ever-Changing World Data is the driving force of our society. From the provision of public services to the running of a successful business, society is increasingly dependent upon the ability to process data at scale. The move toward a more digital society has catalyzed life-improving innovations. But it also means that progress increasingly depends on access to immediately deployable, secure, and reliable digital technologies. Palantir is committed to meeting this need. Our customers process their data in our platforms to confront some of the most important challenges of our time: from revolutionizing healthcare, to fighting global hunger, to shaping the future of mobility. Many of these challenges require our customers to be alert and resilient in times of fundamental insecurity and unrest. They also often operate in a sphere in which the boundaries between the achievement of private and public goals are increasingly blurry. As a software company, we are thus confronted with the urgent and understandable question of how to enable the use of our platforms for processing data, while also enabling our customers to retain full custody and control over that data. In this blog post, we discuss how Palantir defines digital sovereignty and why enabling digital sovereignty plays such an important role in our software development. Most importantly, we want to highlight the investments Palantir is making today to help our customers meet the regulatory and geopolitical demands of tomorrow. Digital sovereignty Digital sovereignty works across two planes: regulatory and geopolitical. And even though the term digital sovereignty has become common parlance, the term’s meaning is still fundamentally contested. There are those who suggest sovereignty can only be achieved through a protectionist stance, that only technology built domestically should be used to process sovereign and economically sensitive data. For these people, sovereignty means autarky. But in light of the speed of social and economic progress, the idea of using only technology built domestically appears illusory. Digital or not, nearly every innovative piece of technology draws inspiration, or even concrete components, from existing technologies developed elsewhere. The impressively fast development of COVID-19 vaccines, among others, has once again demonstrated the benefits of international collaboration. Choosing not to build from existing innovations would not only be a mistake; in light of the urgent challenges our societies confront today, it would also be an irresponsible waste of time. Sovereignty is ultimately defined by the ability to act, which increasingly depends on the ability to analyze data at scale, and then to translate the analysis-informed decisions into operational outcomes. But in order to act autonomously in a digital world, organizations need to be in full control of their data and decision making.
