Retraining models within most AI architectures remains a challenge due to the scarcity of existing data and the wide variance in identified features across the image. Limited uplink bandwidth: Communication with satellites is typically highly asymmetric. Bandwidth constraint means network throughput ranges from GBs for downlink to a few MBs for uplink per pass of the satellite, posing a significant challenge to updating satellite software. To tackle these unique deployment constraints, we introduced the following innovations to Edge AI: Image Pre-processing Drawing on lessons learned from prototyping the unique 4-band, single channel raw image data on board a satellite the previous summer, we invested in a robust pre-processing solution to improve model accuracy without retraining. We developed a custom image registration service that can take in images from the multispectral camera and efficiently process them into 3-channel RGB imagery. We can intentionally ignore the NIR data since our models don’t require it. In practice, this means a capture of dozens of frames yield a handful of RGB images that we can run our models on. When the registration process is finished, we have the full 3-channel RGB image to pass to downstream models. This allows us to plug in third-party models trained for standard RGB images, bypassing the intricacies of the satellite sensor. Fault Tolerance With this launch, we are introducing a new, highly fault-tolerant design for Palantir’s Edge AI system. We carefully considered each aspect of the system across the stack, from the underlying hardware to the architecture of the data pipeline, to achieve better reliability guarantees. On the software side we leveraged Edge AI’s modularity — each of our individual services guarantees data validity as data flows through the pipeline, dynamically purging invalid data in the process. These services are backed by a checkpointing system based in an external storage module attached to the Jetson. Combined with our data integrity logic, this checkpointing system allows Edge AI to recover state and seamlessly resume processing from where it left off in the event of unexpected termination without any user intervention. On the throughput side, we take full advantage of multicore processing. Palantir’s modular design enables the saturation of Edge AI’s pipelines in mere seconds, dramatically increasing throughput. AI Integration Palantir’s Edge AI platform provides a robust framework for orchestrating the multiple AI models on board the satellite. Once pre-processing is complete, we can start running a variety of models against our formed image. Along with our own in-house models, we are excited to have numerous third-party models on board: Palantir Omni: A multi-class computer vision (CV) model capable of identifying land, sea, and air vehicles as well as buildings. Palantir Overcast: A highly performant cloud detector. Xailient: A fast, lightweight ship detector. Pilot.ai: A highly performant, lightweight model for detecting aircraft and ships. Mind Foundry: An ultra low-power image segmentation model that identifies terrain types such as forest and ocean. Our Edge AI platform adapts the input image according to each model’s requirements and stores relevant inferences. Our downstream post-processing services then use this information to generate additional output. Edge AI is capable of sequencing multiple models in parallel. For example, we can run Overcast, MindFoundry, and Omni in sequence. The segmentation model can ignore the clouds identified by Overcast, leading to improvements in segmentation accuracy. Next, these segmentation results can be used by Omni to improve its recall by removing false positives, a major advantage of Edge AI. By allowing models to complement each other with our best-in-class capabilities, we can realize significant improvements in model performance. Post Processing Once the models have finished generating their onboard insights, we post-process the outputs to prepare them for downlink. Projections. All of the models accompanying Edge AI return inferences in pixel space. To locate these inferences in the real world, we operate a projection service downstream of the models that can take in satellite telemetry information and convert inferences from pixel coordinates to geodetic coordinates. This service integrates with global elevation datasets to ensure accurate projections when capturing images over areas with a high variance in elevation. We also account for geometric simplifications of the Earth’s model within the telemetry data that are then rectified when we perform projections. Finally, the service can also correct for satellite telemetry sensor biases over time. These refinements allow us to locate inferences on the Earth more accurately than what raw telemetry would permit. Thumbnails. For each particular inference of interest, we generate lightweight PNG thumbnails which are significantly smaller in size and faster to downlink than the full image. For example, in an image over water we can downlink only the ships identified by the models, greatly reducing our network throughput requirements. Once these processes have finished, we are ready to downlink our outputs. In-Orbit Upgrade Infrastructure Due to uplink bandwidth constraints, we developed a custom upgrade framework to handle in-orbit updates. Instead of shipping a new version of our software to the satellite, we can compute and ship an optimized package that encodes the differences between the new version and the current version installed on the satellite. Once on board, our upgrade infrastructure can reconstruct the new version of our software before instantiating the Edge AI system. This upgrade capability extends to our models; we can retrain models on the ground and update model weights in orbit as needed, continually improving the onboard AI capabilities. Security We have implemented various cryptographic mechanisms to validate the data sent down by the satellite and so that only Palantir-authorized updates can happen on board the satellite. This ensures the integrity of our communications which is especially important since we do not control all the hops in the network. Satellogic mission operations utilize different cryptographic tools to ensure the privacy, integrity, and security of the communications, both for TT&C and data transfers to and from the ground. What’s next? As we look to future launches, we are considering new capabilities we could add to our current offering. Here’s a quick overview of what’s next: Georegistration: We are committed to achieving sub-10m accuracy for our inferences on board the satellite. Satellite telemetry data can only get us within hundreds of meters of the actual inference’s location due to onboard sensor inaccuracies. We’re excited to announce that Palantir’s new in-house georegistration capabilities will be part of our next Edge AI system launch. Our georegistration software is already processing downlinked satellite images, but we are working on integrating this capability into our in-orbit system through Edge AI’s modular interface to dramatically improve our in-orbit inference accuracy. Hardware security: At Palantir, we view security as an ever-moving target. To best protect our edge deployments against constantly evolving threats, we are planning to introduce new hardware-backed security mechanisms on board the next generation of our Edge AI system for satellites. These will complement our existing mechanisms and allow us to offer stronger guarantees around confidentiality and integrity for our Edge AI system. Tasking support: We are working closely with Satellogic to create capabilities for more granular control of our Edge AI system through the Palantir MetaConstellation software. Beyond system upgrades, we are looking to dynamically adapt Edge AI’s processing to upcoming mission requirements, taking latency, power budgets, and bandwidth constraints into account to configure models for improved accuracy depending on the expected imagery data. Stay tuned for more on our new tasking functionality. ISLs and Upgraded Comms: For future launches, we are investigating more communication options including Inter-Satellite Links (ISL). These will enable low latency autonomous tipping and cueing between our Edge AI-enabled satellites, including cross-constellation tasking, all done at the edge. This is a revolutionary capability that we are laying the foundation for with our current Edge AI work. Foundry Deployability to the Edge: We are continuing to invest in a framework that enable seamless integration with our Foundry platform. This will enable users to author logic and models in Foundry, then utilize our Apollo delivery platform to push that model up to a satellite. We currently provide this functionality in ground-based environments but are excited to expand to space. This integration is crucial to us to enable CI/CD of models all the way to the edge. Conclusion For years, our customers have used Palantir software to process satellite imagery on the ground. We have continually worked to bring this processing closer to the edge to better support our customers’ mission areas and operations. The Palantir-Satellogic collaboration represents a significant step in expediting delivery and dramatically improving the quality of data sent back to customers. This pioneering application of Edge AI in space aims to serve as the foundation for advanced analytics that can inform timely solutions to address critical global priorities, like combatting climate change, preventing disasters, and improving emergency response. title: From Customer to Coder
description: UK Royal Navy Officer Reflects on Palantir Fellowship Experience
author: Palantir
body: From Customer to Coder UK Royal Navy officer reflects on Palantir fellowship experience As part of Palantir’s ongoing mission to champion the UK Armed Forces and upskill personnel for the future of defence, Palantir is proud to participate in the Percy Hobart Fellowship. The 12-week Fellowship is run by PUBLIC on behalf of the UK Ministry of Defence and offers a training placement for Royal Navy and Royal Air Force officials, officers, and NCOs. Fellows are paired with some of the most cutting-edge companies in science and technology and are offered mentoring, workshops, and course material to supplement their placements. The immersive, hands-on experience in innovation and technology equips fellows with lessons they can bring back to their Services to enhance innovation across defence. In this post, Royal Navy Warrant Officer Class 2 (WO2) Rob Dye reflects on how his 12 weeks at Palantir offered him unparalleled insights into Palantir’s structure, workflows, and goals, taking him from customer to coder on a range of exciting projects. UK Royal Navy Warrant Officer Rob Dye When offered a 12-week placement with Palantir as part of the Royal Navy sponsored Percy Hobart innovation fellowship I couldn’t accept quickly enough. I joined the Royal Marines 20 years ago, straight from school, and have become accustomed to the structure and culture that comes with military life. So, the chance to work inside an innovative tech organisation was like the gift I had always wanted but was too afraid to ask for. Palantir wasn’t a new organisation to me. As the Technical Lead for the Royal Navy’s Project KRAKEN, which uses Foundry as the foundation for personnel management, amongst other workflows, I’ve been a customer of Palantir’s for the past six months. I’ve experienced first-hand how Palantir’s customer focused approach means they’ve been able to meet any challenges I’ve thrown at them. But while the company was generally a known entity, I wasn’t expecting how welcomed I would be in the workplace. Being at Palantir gave me a chance to see just how the company’s culture, ethos, and continual feedback loops between business and product development teams truly enables those challenges to be met. During my time, I’ve been fortunate enough to support and build solutions for several deployments across the organisation. From government to charities, Palantir supported my experience with assistance from the teams around me to quickly add value and meet the customer requirements. My first experience building in Foundry saw me build an OSINT dashboard for an elephant conservation organisation. With advice from experienced Palantirians, I was able to ingest the raw data, clean and display visually for the customer in a choropleth map, meaning they could easily visualise incidents over time by region and begin integrating with additional data sources already in the platform. Now, that’s not to say my first attempt was perfect. But through direct customer feedback I was able to quickly amend the dashboards to suit their needs and deliver business value. Collaboration was the key to success. Lessons learned: ‘If you can’t figure something out in 10 minutes, ask someone’ It is no secret that defence is deeply compartmentalised. Coming from this structure and stepping into this new environment took some adaption, both mentally and culturally. As I joined Palantir for onboarding, I was shocked with how willingly people reached out from across the whole organisation to say hello, discuss their experiences, and offer help or advice. I soon realised this was not a one-off experience, but was deeply rooted in Palantir’s culture. People are genuinely encouraged to reach out. The best bit of advice I was given throughout my 12 weeks was that if you that if you cannot figure something out in under 10 minutes, ask someone, because there will almost definitely be someone around you who has experienced your problem before — and solved it. This isn’t to say everything always works, but there is a strong, well-practiced process in the company to ensure teams sit down and ask why something didn’t work and why something failed. I experienced this first hand when I joined a 5-whys session for a US forestry deployment focused on fire fighting, as the team established the root cause for why a cluster had been allowed to reach a critical point before resolution. The willingness across teams to interrogate mistakes, to make sure learnings are assessed and taken seriously, stops others from making the same mistakes. Doing the uncomfortable, often difficult, work of evaluating errors builds better teams and strengthens outputs for the long haul. So, what’s next as I move back to defence and what are my big three learnings from Palantir? Failure should be embraced; we only learn through understanding our failures, finding the root cause and putting processes in place to make sure they do not happen again. Transparency through communication is key; without a transparent, open organisation you will lack trust and work will be conducted in isolation for fear of upsetting the applecart. Adopting a flat structure doesn’t mean there isn’t a hierarchy or people will go rogue; rather, it means teams will have the space to grow and won’t be afraid to try new things because there is no such thing as a bad idea, just a failure to try. To learn more about how Palantir is driving Defence’s digital transformation and career opportunities, please visit our webpage.

title: Palantir Foundry and Accenture Expertise: Powerful results
description: Unlocking the value of data in day-to-day operations
author: Palantir
body: Palantir Foundry and Accenture Expertise: Powerful results In the past few years, companies have had to learn how to navigate an increasingly volatile world rife with conflict, disruptions, and instability. Doing so requires finding new ways to remain agile and resilient against rapidly changing circumstances. Palantir and Accenture have worked with enterprises around the world to accomplish this, largely by unlocking the value of the data inherent in day-to-day operations. The Value of Answers What would it look like, for decision makers to have near-instant answers to questions that span the entire breadth of global enterprises, from the supply of raw materials to finished goods in consumer hands and everything in between? Today, many of the answers to these questions all exist in the form of data. However due to the complexity and scale of modern businesses, the answers are inaccessible in incompatible formats, siloed systems, and more. Yet it has never before been as critically important to have full visibility across an enterprise. For example, every few weeks, supply chains can be broken due to labor shortages, trade regionalization, port congestion, and so much more. Course correcting in the face of these increasingly frequent disruptions requires a near-real-time holistic view of your organization, insights on how events ripple out to impact adjacent nodes in your chain, and the capability to operationalize the insights garnered from these insights. Powerful Partnership Palantir and Accenture have both worked to provide innovative solutions that empower their clients to help meet these challenges head on. We’re now excited to announce a new partnership between Palantir and Accenture. Highlighting the force multiplier Palantir Foundry represents to Accenture’s clients, Accenture Applied Intelligence is working with Palantir to build an innovation center — the Accenture Palantir Studio — housing over 1000 experts on Foundry who will build and design new cutting edge solutions. With the creation of this new innovation center, Accenture will be expanding their capabilities in Palantir Foundry to bring newfound value to their clients. Palantir Foundry is the operating system for the modern enterprise, grounding data, analytics, and business teams in a common foundation. With flexible deployment that can meet companies wherever they are in their digital transformation journey, Foundry provides value from day one, taking the operationalization of data from months to days. Accenture Applied Intelligence has a strong track record of driving data-powered AI and analytics solutions from customer engagement to pricing and B2B growth. Accenture also brings deep expertise in a broad diversity of industries and contextual know-how on specific business processes, expediting the integration of a software-defined data platform like Foundry. “This alliance with Palantir will enhance how we integrate disparate datasets, ensure high data quality and richness, and apply new AI techniques to solve big problems — helping our clients get better insights and decisioning capabilities.” said Sanjeev Vohra, global lead, Accenture Applied Intelligence. Expanding Horizons The intricate world of enterprise data plumbing (integrating complex datasets, systems, and applications) demands solutions that can be deployed across an organization, adapt to a rapidly changing world, and enable users to configure workflows and use cases in hours or days rather than months or years. With this new key partnership, Accenture will be able to merge its industry, data, and AI expertise with Foundry’s powerful capabilities to not only help equip enterprises to face the new challenges of today, but also to power the growth of tomorrow. title: The Challenges of Building an Architecture from Scratch
description: One of our Foundry for Builders partners shares why they decided to build on Foundry
author: Palantir
body: The Challenges of Building an Architecture from Scratch One of our Foundry for Builders partners shares why they decided to build on Foundry There’s no shortage of foundational decisions that startups and other emerging companies need to make at an early stage, especially when it comes to building a technical stack that can support future development efforts and business goals. When internal resources are sacred and generating value quickly is critical, startups must be data-driven and efficient at their core. After all, speed-to-value could mean the difference between winning and losing altogether. Building a truly resilient and flexible tech stack is no small endeavor. Companies hire dozens or hundreds of engineers and spend years building infrastructure platforms to scale their businesses — just ask us. When we started to ideate on Foundry, our technology platform for operational decision-making, we realized that the core building blocks we needed simply weren’t available on the market. Sure, there were open source tools out there, but they were narrowly focused and didn’t work for deployment models beyond a single cloud. Moreover, piecing together a patchwork was too brittle for scaling a high growth business, and it didn’t give our engineers and operators any real lift when responding to cross-cutting issues. So, we decided to build the entire toolkit we needed ourselves. As it turns out, what we thought would take a few months took us five years of intensive R&D to create. Confronting uncertainty One of the key tenets Palantir kept in mind while building Foundry was that the world is infinitely complex, with problems and solutions in constant flux. Our open architecture is purpose-built for this kind of environment — and as it so happens, the environments of our startup customers and day zero partners tend to have significant uncertainty and risk. To learn more about what a startup looks like from the inside and why even small companies might choose to build on Foundry, we asked one of our Foundry for Builders partners to weigh in. Below, Gelu Vrabi, VP of Engineering at VayuAI, gives us a first-hand take on what his company’s needs were and why VayuAI decided to build on Foundry. What were your considerations when building a technical foundation for your business? The main considerations for anyone trying to build the data infrastructure for their business will always be development time (which affects revenue as well as costs, since more time means more developer hours), cost of the services or software used, and what is usually referred to as “technical debt” — or, more accurately, the scalability of the solution. Nothing scales perfectly with zero cost, so this is more of a spectrum. I would say the main advantages of Foundry are in improving scalability through the way data processing and access is managed in the data ontology, as well as either reducing development time compared to building from scratch, or cost compared to more niche solutions that tend to cover only part of the infrastructure landscape. How does Foundry’s ontological layer make your data infrastructure more efficient and secure? One way that Foundry makes an engineer’s life much easier is simply managing permissions, which the ontology makes much easier. Any organization dealing with a significant number of users and data complexity will need to build internal tools that basically replicate the data ontology in Foundry. Enterprises need to be able to see the data lineage (including the data processing code), control how much access to the underlying data a user has, and permitting users to request access and discover what they need access to themselves. So, the data ontology is essential tooling that is not easy to build but greatly improves the security and efficiency of your data infrastructure. Did you set out to build a data foundation to solve a single business problem? How did your chosen data foundation adapt to changing business needs? At Vayu, we had a few business problems that we were trying to optimize for in the beginning, as we have both an IIoT solution that has its own challenges and requirements, as well as a more typical SaaS offering that is partly integrated with the IIoT solution but also offers other types of services, like data aggregation and simulation-on-demand. But on top of all this, what you almost always find when running a business is that you have new requirements, or at least new opportunities, that always come with increased complexity for your data infrastructure. In view of this ever-increasing complexity, flexibility is crucial. We’ve found that the improved scalability (both technically and in terms of managing complexity) that Foundry offers is a great enabler. The Palantir SaaS solution grows and evolves alongside our customers. How complex was your data landscape before Foundry? How many source systems did you need to connect? Prior to Foundry, we were mainly storing data in a data lake and a few RDS databases in AWS. There were a few sources for this data, such as our IIoT devices, our cloud simulations, third party services/APIs, and user-uploaded data. Which point solutions did you avoid purchasing because you had comparable functionality already in Foundry? On the data exploration and visualization side, Foundry removes the need to purchase and use separate products like Excel and Tableau or deal with lower level infrastructure constructs like EC2 instances and Sagemaker Notebook instances. Since all the tools are on the same platform, they integrate much more deeply with the data stores than these alternatives. This makes the whole process more efficient (no importing or copying-and-pasting data into Excel, no database credentials and querying into Tableau, etc.). I’ve mentioned some of the pros and cons compared to our approach (which was leaning more towards building from scratch) and other potential options, but one thing I wanted to highlight in particular is Foundry’s toolkit for visualization, which includes products like Slate or Contour. These tools are really a huge enabler for Vayu compared to the other options on the market. In contrast with something like Tableau, the ease of use and deep integration of some of the “simpler” tools in Foundry can really enhance the ability of non-technical stakeholders to access and consume data. Even more impactful for us, Slate, an application-builder, enables us to develop our SaaS offering far faster and cheaper than building a web application from scratch. Focus on what matters Though no two organizations are quite the same, we’ve heard many companies like VayuAI emphasize the importance of building on top of a platform that has a massive range of functionality out of the box, in one environment. Regardless of size, companies should focus ruthlessly on building the business or the product that sets them apart, that differentiates them from the rest of the market, and that allows them to do so faster. VayuAI’s experience shows that three of the things that matter to many tech-forward organizations are scalability, flexibility, and reducing integration complexity. When VayuAI first decided to use Foundry, the company already had a complicated data infrastructure that would only get more complex, so it needed a solution that could scale over time. Palantir’s Foundry platform enables not only scalability, but also configurability: Foundry can easily adapt to new or modified workflows, interface configurations, emerging data and technology availability, and changes to regulations or governance models. Finally, Foundry was designed for use by both technical and non-technical users; people can collaborate over business logic, algorithms, code, formulas, spreadsheets, using built-in, user-friendly applications while also contributing their decisions and learnings back into the ontology. Foundry’s fully managed cloud environment enables organizations to derive long-term value quickly from a rapidly deployable commercial platform, while avoiding the significant hidden costs and compounding technical debt that often arise with custom development and patchwork solutions. Dr. Karp speaks to the differentiation companies see by building in Foundry From managing data across jurisdictions to developing advanced digital twin simulations, Palantir CEO Alex Karp discusses how we’ve purpose-built our software to handle disruption and dislocation. Watch the full video.

title: How Palantir Foundry Extends Your Data Platforms
description: Data platforms yield insights — Foundry fuels decisions
author: Palantir
body: How Palantir Foundry Extends Your Data Platforms Data platforms yield insights — Foundry fuels decisions By Akshay Krishnaswamy, Chief Architect, Palantir Editor’s note: This post is the first installment in a series discussing how Palantir Foundry complements existing solutions within enterprise software architectures. Palantir Foundry is sometimes incorrectly thought of as a data platform solution. In a way, this confusion is understandable. For organizations that are earlier in the digital journey, Foundry can serve this purpose — providing key functionality such as data integration, management, governance, and search and analysis. Foundry’s focus, however, extends beyond those capabilities toward its ultimate aim: enhancing the operational decisions that constitute an enterprise. While data platforms do important work in centralizing and managing data in a single place, Foundry is designed to connect analytics to operations — continuously and dynamically in a complex world. As a result, it is best thought of as an operating system that coordinates the interplay of data, models, and decisions in an enterprise. This orientation requires a different architecture. Below, we discuss how Foundry’s capabilities can dramatically extend the traditional value proposition of a data platform, building operational connectivity. Data Platforms Yield Insights Data platforms — like Snowflake, Google BigQuery, AWS Redshift, IBM Db2, Azure Synapse, Teradata, etc. — are ideal for consolidating large volumes of data from multiple sources, providing structure, and deriving insights. In a fast-changing world subject to significant macro shocks, however, many organizations see the need to move beyond insight delivery: They want to give decision makers the technological levers to take action. In practice, this means enabling decisions across functions to be simulated, implemented in underlying systems, and cycled back into a common data foundation for feedback-driven improvement. Given the complexity of today’s operating environments, software needs to coordinate decisions in ways that are both dynamic (i.e., agile in response to changing external conditions) and scalable (i.e., optimized across teams, regions, and even business units). This capacity requires capabilities that reside outside of traditional data platforms — such as model integration, a dynamic semantic layer, rapid application building, and decision simulation and write-back. Palantir Foundry Fuels Decisions Foundry is designed for deep operational connectivity — empowering organizations to close the loop between their data, analytics, and operational decisions. To fuel operational connectivity, Foundry extends your existing data platforms with capability stacks that include model integration, dynamic ontologies, modular workflows, and decision orchestration. Palantir Foundry can extend your organization’s data platform into the operational sphere in four key ways: Model / AI Integration & Creation Model development and integration in Foundry is a first-class set of capabilities, spanning the entire MLOps lifecycle. It integrates machine learning, artificial intelligence, statistical, and mathematical models with other components of the Foundry ecosystem, allowing models to be chained together and operationalized across diverse workflows. This layer’s core capabilities include the ability to develop, discover, manage, and deploy models. Automated, software-defined integrations rapidly connect data and models outside of Foundry. Connections can be made via native platform integrations (e.g., AWS Sagemaker, Azure ML, DataRobot, Databricks) or by importing your model artifact directly into Foundry as code, libraries, or trained models. Support for all major open-source frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, and SKLearn — as well as interoperability standards (ONNX) — streamlines integrations. Foundry Code Workbooks enable native, secure data access for model builders using dataset and ontology paradigms as they perform end-to-end model development. Foundry Model Management offers ongoing evaluation and monitoring of deployed and candidate models, as well as multi-stakeholder approval and release processes for deploying improvements into operations. Foundry features full versioning, branching, reproducibility, security, and lineage for your integrated data and models. Model Objectives, a “mission control” for models used in Foundry workflows, ensure that your business logic is tied to specific business KPIs and deployed for a consistent purpose across use cases. Dynamic Ontology & Semantic Layer Foundry integrates all relevant data, logic, and models into a digital representation of your organization, called an ontology. The ontology goes beyond business objects and relationships, encoding advanced data semantics (spatial, relational, temporal), “kinetics” (reflecting complex chains of write-operations and system integrations), and granular permissions — all exposed via both UIs and secure APIs. An ontology is quick to bootstrap, and typically grows over time with new workflows, capturing additional data sources, objects, relationships, interactions, and processes. A digital representation of your business reflects both the key semantics of your world (objects and relations) as well as the key kinetics of your world (functions, actions, and models). Decision and data capture ensures that workflows can scale without fracturing the core data foundation, which will continue to serve as a trustworthy source of truth for the enterprise. Native “scenario-aware” functionality allows for what-if analysis and running compound simulations. Modular Workflows & Applications Foundry includes a rich set of building blocks for quickly assembling workflows and read-write operational applications (versus simple read-only dashboards). These include the semantic and kinetic primitives discussed above, allowing your teams to configure high-quality interactive workflows for frontline users in hours. No/low-code application builders leverage the ontology and provide a highly-flexible framework for users to interact with your organization’s data asset, while managing the underlying storage, compute, ontological data, model bindings, and security paradigm. WYSIWYG, widget-driven builders offer interaction with both ontological data, as well as tabular/SQL-shaped data. “Low floor & high ceiling” flexibility allows you to build anything from spartan applications for a small group, to mission-critical applications at the core of operations centers. Open APIs ensure the platform accommodates an evolving technology landscape. Decision Orchestration This layer provides the technical bridge between your organization’s analytics and its operational workflows. As operators, business processes, and systems make decisions and take action, this layer writes the results back into the ontology, providing feedback loops for high-velocity organizational learning. Extensible, bidirectional connectors allow Foundry to record and write back all decisions to your organization’s ontology as well as to its operational/transactional systems (e.g., ERP, CRM, MES, Asset Config, Edge). Foundry maintains a complete log of both decisions and states to ensure auditability and full transparency. Simulations give users access to powerful “what-if” analysis and decision exploration, enabling them to simulate possible actions and evaluate how they would affect the business. Simulations can be tactical or long-lived, refreshing along with data and models. Full lineage is maintained from data to decision, allowing you to ask, “What was the state of the world?” when a particular piece of data or metadata was written externally. Decisions are always non-destructive since Foundry brings in underlying data through system integrations and versions all changes. These capabilities animate a unique form of operational connectivity that drives success across industries — from the World Food Programme delivering life-saving assistance, to pricing optimization at a large beverage company, to inventory optimization at a global manufacturer, and many more. Looking to close the loop between analytics and operations? Working with a data platform we didn’t mention? Get in touch with a member of our Foundry product team.

title: Sarcos & Palantir
description: Palantir and Sarcos Robotics & Technology Corporation are pushing the boundaries of modern edge operations, combining Sarcos robotics with Palantir Edge.
author: Palantir
body: Palantir Robotics Edge Computing AI Partnerships Sarcos & Palantir Pushing the Future of AI and Robotics to the Edge Palantir 5 min read · Apr 20, 2022 -- Listen Share Press enter or click to view image in full size Palantir’s collaboration with Sarcos Robotics & Technology Corporation (Sarcos) is pushing the boundaries of modern edge operations by combining the strength of Sarcos robotic systems with the edge capabilities of Palantir software. Palantir is focused on helping Sarcos stream high volume sensor data from their robots in real-time, run complex AI algorithms at the edge, and continuously deploy software updates to their fleet at scale, no matter how remote or disconnected the environment. As Sarcos deploys its two flagship robots — the Guardian® XO ® and the Guardian® XT TM — to an increasing number of customer environments and industries worldwide, computing at the edge reliably and efficiently is key. The Guardian XO robot is a full-body powered industrial exoskeleton, offered via Robot-as-a-Service (RaaS) lease, that multiplies worker productivity while mitigating occupational injury and fatigue. The Guardian XT robot is a teleoperated dexterous robotic system that extends human capability in complex industrial environments (like shipbuilding, power line maintenance or pipe inspection), reducing the need for humans to work in risky or dangerous environments. Palantir’s Edge offerings can enhance the operations of Sarcos robots as follows: Palantir Edge Streaming: With Edge Streaming, Sarcos knows exactly what is happening with its robots at all times. Sarcos can stream data from approximately 125 sensors on each robot to the Palantir Foundry platform in real-time, enabling high volume data integration and analysis, driving rapid iteration and product development cycles. Sarcos is able to parse data collected and pull only what is needed from the robots, which can reduce the costs and latency involved in shipping terabytes of data to the cloud. Get Palantir ’s stories in your inbox Join Medium for free to get updates from this writer. Subscribe Subscribe Remember me for faster sign in Palantir Edge AI: Sarcos can integrate AI models fleet-wide across edge devices with Palantir Edge AI. Metadata from edge-deployed models flow back into the organization’s core AI/ML infrastructure, accelerating Sarcos’ work toward autonomy through model retraining, offering long-term, reliable maintenance of edge-deployed AI models. Users can seamlessly scale AI models across remote, disconnected edge nodes with real-time sensor, video and/or audio data. Palantir Apollo for the Edge: Sarcos can scale its fleet of robots by enabling continuous deployment of software updates from the single Palantir Apollo control layer. Apollo for the Edge provides homogenous control of heterogenous environments, where edge device requirements may differ based on location or customer need. The Apollo platform helps manage Edge Streaming and Edge AI technology, ensuring all devices are operating with the latest updates at all times, anywhere in the world. Sarcos is focused on creating the most productive, cost-effective workforce in the world and its unique approach to AI technology helps support that vision. Sarcos is developing AI algorithms to unlock a new level of efficiency and adaptability for its robots by modeling the way humans learn rather than relying on high volume training data and tedious repetition. Sarcos robotic systems can mimic the actions of the human operator, building up operations in stages with a “task library” approach that has the potential to transform commercial robotics by removing the need to reprogram a robot with each new business need. Palantir’s Edge technology can extend this capability to robots in any environment with continuous integration/continuous deployment (CI/CD) of AI models all the way to the edge. Palantir Foundry can also help organizations transform internal business operations by optimizing shipment and coordination of hardware parts, avoiding production stalls and streamlining spend. Palantir aims to serve as the operating system for a growing number of companies seeking to automate their processes and workflows. Successful automation will continue to be a critical competitive advantage in the evolving industry 4.0 landscape, where interconnectivity and smart automation are paramount. “What makes the Sarcos and Palantir relationship so unique is the fact that we’re really pushing that technology curve. It’s the advancement that [Sarcos is] making in AI, machine learning and cloud compute, and it’s [Foundry] that allows us to be able to run those models and really understand what’s happening with the robot real time.” -Sarcos CEO Kiva Allgood As Sarcos robots are distributed to a growing number of unstructured environments, operating seamlessly at the edge and progressing toward increased autonomy is crucial. Palantir’s software platforms and edge offerings directly address these needs and support Sarcos’s vision to revolutionize the workforce. Together, Palantir and Sarcos are augmenting human capability and charting the future of robotics and AI at the edge.
