Palantir ontwikkelt software waarmee onze klanten hun eigen gegevens legaal, veilig en efficiënt kunnen verwerken. We houden ons niet bezig met surveillance of spionage. Palantir-producten hebben unieke eigenschappen die onder andere interessant zijn voor inlichtingendiensten. De klant blijft altijd verplicht om een juridische inschatting te maken van het legale gebruik van de software gezien de autoriteit en het doel ervan. Palantir staat niet toe dat de software wordt gebruikt in strijd met de toepasselijke wetgeving. Hoe zit het met geruchten dat Palantir predictive-policing mogelijk maakt — is dit waar? Nee. Palantir biedt geen tools voor voorspellend politiewerk. Palantir stelt wereldwijd aan politiediensten software ter beschikking waarmee zij hun reguliere opsporingswerk efficiënter en volgens de geldende richtlijnen en procedures kunnen uitvoeren. Waarom bood Palantir haar diensten gratis aan tijdens de COVID-19-crisis? In sommige gevallen heeft Palantir haar software pro bono aangeboden in de strijd tegen COVID-19 omdat we onze ervaring, expertise en software wilden inzetten om snel te helpen bij een van de grootste wereldwijde uitdagingen van de afgelopen decennia. Palantir werd wereldwijd bij verschillende instanties en partners ingezet om een geïntegreerde aanpak en reactie op de pandemie te ondersteunen. Op deze manier hebben we ervoor kunnen zorgen dat de besluitvormers van onze partners in bijna-realtime beschikken over alle relevante informatie in de strijd tegen COVID-19. Om een voorbeeld te schetsen: onze software wordt momenteel gebruikt door het Amerikaanse ministerie van Volksgezondheid (HHS) in het HHS Protect-programma en door de National Health Service (NHS) in het Verenigd Koninkrijk. Met HHS Protect worden meer dan 150 verschillende databronnen verzameld in één ecosysteem. Dit project integreert gegevens van federale, staats- en lokale overheden en de gezondheidsindustrie om een holistisch beeld van het gezondheidssysteem mogelijk te maken. Ons systeem maakt het mogelijk om dergelijke data te verenigen en organiseren. De data blijven bewaard bij de respectievelijke eigenaren zonder dat wij of andere buitenstaanders er toegang toe hebben. Bij de NHS in het VK werd Foundry op zijn beurt gebruikt om de vraag en het aanbod van beschermende uitrusting in realtime vast te leggen en te delen met verschillende instellingen. Ziekenhuizen kunnen hun individuele behoeften van dag tot dag kenbaar maken en zo de toewijzing van levensreddende apparatuur — bijv. ventilatoren — beheren en de toewijzing van benodigdheden optimaliseren waar patiënten ze het meest nodig hebben. De ontwikkelde oplossing omvat een directe integratie van reeds bestaande systemen voor het beheer van voorraden. Hierdoor kon de administratieve inspanning van NHS-medewerkers minimaal blijven. Nog een voorbeeld waar we bijzonder trots op zijn, is hoe we onze partner The World Food Programme konden ondersteunen tijdens de pandemie. Wereldwijd maken humanitaire organisaties gebruik van WFPs logistieke keten om noodgezondheidszorg en humanitaire hulp te leveren. Met behulp van onze software heeft WFP meer dan 148.000 kubieke meter levensreddende gezondheids- en humanitaire vracht weten te leveren in 173 verschillende landen, namens 72 verschillende organisaties. Waarom steunt Palantir het GAIA-X-initiatief, dat tot doel heeft de digitale soevereiniteit van Europa te versterken? Palantirs medeoprichter en CEO, Dr. Alex Karp, heeft vaak zijn bewondering uitgesproken voor de sociale markteconomie in Europa en voor de traditie en enorme expertise van de Europese industrie. We zien onszelf als een partner voor gevestigde Europese bedrijven en willen hen volgen op het pad naar digitale transformatie. De onderling verbonden, veilige open data-infrastructuur waar GAIA-X naar streeft, zal hier een grote stap voorwaarts zijn. Sinds onze oprichting in het begin van deze eeuw hebben we problemen aangepakt die tevens relevant zijn voor GAIA-X. Bijvoorbeeld: hoe kunnen instellingen in de publieke en private sector de gedistribueerde, heterogene hoeveelheden gegevens beoordelen die ze gedurende tientallen jaren hebben verzameld? Hoe kunnen organisaties gegevens efficiënt gebruiken en tegelijkertijd over organisatiegrenzen heen samenwerken zonder de gegevensbeveiliging en gegevensbescherming in gevaar te brengen? Na meer dan 17 jaar werkzaam te zijn in zeer complexe, sterk gereguleerde dataomgevingen, hebben we ruime ervaring opgebouwd in het afstemmen van technologische oplossingen op richtlijnen voor databeheer, wettelijke bepalingen en andere normatieve randvoorwaarden. Juist deze ervaring en competentie willen wij bijdragen aan het GAIA-X project. Hoe maakt Palantir veilige samenwerking tussen organisaties mogelijk? Skywise is een mooi voorbeeld van hoe onze producten veilige en gecontroleerde samenwerking mogelijk maken binnen organisaties en over organisatiegrenzen heen. Skywise is een digitaal ecosysteem voor de hele luchtvaartindustrie, aangeboden door Airbus en gebaseerd op Palantir Foundry. Luchtvaartmaatschappijen en leveranciers in de luchtvaartindustrie gebruiken Skywise wereldwijd om de operationele efficiëntie en veiligheid te verbeteren en vertragingen te voorkomen. Zo kunnen leveranciers hun voorraden optimaliseren en late leveringen verminderen. Airbus versnelt de productie en ontwikkeling van nieuwe bedrijfsmodellen. Skywise brengt verschillende organisaties samen in één ecosysteem. Deze samenwerking wordt mogelijk gemaakt door middel van een uniforme data-integratiearchitectuur waarbij de deelnemers hun eigen verenigde informatie kunnen beheren en samenwerken aan een specifiek doel door specifieke gegevens op een veilige manier te kunnen uitwisselen. Zou Palantir het gebruik van software om ethische redenen ooit beperken? Ja. Palantir heeft dit vele malen gedaan. Onder andere in een artikel in de Washington Post (september 2019) onderstreepte onze CEO Dr. Alex Karp de ethische verantwoordelijkheid van het bedrijf om misbruik van de technologie te voorkomen. Palantir is zich zeer bewust van de ethische verantwoordelijkheid die we als bedrijf hebben om misbruik van onze technologie te voorkomen. Palantir werkt doorgaans niet samen met klanten of regeringen wiens standpunten of acties wij in strijd achten met onze missie om westerse liberale democratieën en hun strategische bondgenoten te ondersteunen. In alle gevallen evalueren we potentiële klanten en mogelijke toepassingen zorgvuldig op naleving van onze waarden en principes. Zoals we bijvoorbeeld ook duidelijk maakten in onze public filings met de SEC, doet Palantir geen zaken met de Chinese Communistische Partij, host geen platforms in China en legt beperkingen op aan de platform-toegang vanuit China. Ook willen we onze software niet ter beschikking stellen aan de Russische overheid. Palantir heeft ook samenwerkingen met andere internationale overheidsinstanties geweigerd vanwege zorgen over mensenrechtenschendingen. Palantir heeft al vele jaren een toegewijd team dat zich bezighoudt met kwesties op het gebied van gegevensbescherming en gegevensethiek. Meer informatie over Palantirs benadering van Privacy en Civil Liberties Engineering lees je hier. Hoe is het om bij Palantir te werken? Bij het vinden van nieuwe collega’s zoeken we overal naar talent. Om het meeste te bereiken met onze software, heeft Palantir mensen nodig met een breed scala aan achtergronden, perspectieven en levenservaringen. Bij ons werken voormalige artiesten, Olympiërs, operazangers en kernfysici, net als veteranen en industrieleiders. We nemen starters aan, maar ook mensen uit de top van hun vakgebied. Wat ons als Palantirians verenigt, is een niet-aflatende passie en toewijding aan onze missie. Waar je ook bent gevestigd, of in welk team je ook werkt, je maakt deel uit van een groep mensen die samenwerken om oplossingen te bouwen voor de meest belangrijke problemen, in een bedrijf dat de allerbeste ideeën waardeert. Dit is onze engineering culture. Als je enthousiast wordt van werken aan de meest belangrijke problemen ter wereld en de vrijheid wilt om ze op te lossen, dan willen we met jou samenwerken. We hebben momenteel verschillende vacatures uit staan voor ons Nederlandse team. Om je op weg te helpen hebben we hier informatie over de sollicitatieprocedure verzameld. Voor mediavragen kunt u een e-mail sturen naar media@palantir.com. Mocht je na het lezen van deze blog nog vragen over Palantir hebben, kijk dan op onze website www.palantir.com voor meer informatie. Palantir Netherlands: Frequently Asked Questions We on the team at Palantir Netherlands have received many questions about Palantir. Given the high interest in our company, we collected the questions we receive most often and use this blog post to answer them. If you want to solve your organisation’s problems with our software, get in touch with us here. Or do you already know Palantir by name and are you curious what it is like to work with us? Then please read on. We are always looking for sales and engineering talent! What is Palantir? Palantir Technologies is an international software company founded in 2003 in Silicon Valley. Nowadays, our headquarters is located in Denver, Colorado (USA) and we have Palantir offices around the world, including in the Netherlands and London (UK). We build software with the conviction that companies and institutions can change the world for the better with technology that unlocks data and fuels insights. Our customers include large publicly traded companies and government agencies. Palantir’s software is deployed today in more than 50 sectors, for example, in areas of healthcare, automotive, finance, and supply chain. In some countries, we also assist the police and other government agencies responsible for ensuring legal and regulatory compliance, and the safety of people. Where other tech companies might base their business model on collecting or selling data, we base our business on software sales. In that sense we are not a ‘data company’, but a software company. All our products come with built in data protection functionalities that enable our customers to meet strict privacy and security obligations. In this blog you can also read more about how we manage that. Confidentiality is a requirement for some of our clients, particularly in the intelligence and defense spaces. As a result, we are often unable to publicly communicate about a partnership. That also means that we are sometimes criticized for secrecy and faced with claims that we are doing things that we are not actually doing. In this blog we are therefore happy to answer the questions we often receive. What exactly does Palantir do? We develop and sell software for data-driven decision-making and business processes. Our platforms Palantir Foundry and Palantir Gothamcombine data analysis with specific business processes, so that the right data reaches the right users and decision-makers at the right time. In addition, Apollo enables organisations to autonomously manage and continuously deploy software, wherever your business needs it to be. Together our platforms enable advanced analytics, smooth collaboration, and continuous improvement of the customer’s organisation. Is Palantir a software company or a data miner? Palantir is a software company. Our business model is not based on monetizing personal data. Palantir does not collect, analyze or sell customer data for our own purposes. Instead, we develop software platforms and sell software licenses. Our goal is to provide our customers with an operating system so that they can process their own data in accordance with their own rules and goals. Data protection and security are essential to Palantir and are a fundamental part of the architecture. Yet Palantir is sometimes described as a data broker or data collector. Does the company benefit from access to customer data? No. This is a common misconception that is easy to understand because there are so many other companies that do just that. Palantir stands out from that crowd in that we do not collect or sell customer data. In addition, we do not facilitate the exchange of data between customers, unless those customers expressly agree to work together as part of a joint project. We only make data exchange between customers technically possible if both customers have expressly agreed to work together in this regard. Our software and services are used exclusively on behalf of our customers: the customer determines how the data is used. Our customers have full control over where and how analytics are performed. We will not and cannot reuse or transfer our customers’ data for our own purposes. In addition, any collaboration with a customer is completely — contractually, operationally and technologically — separate from all other customer relationships, unless, as mentioned above, our customers expressly ask to enter into a collaboration. Helping our customers be more autonomous has always been central to Palantir’s approach to building technology. Integrating and analyzing data in our platforms is not an end in itself, but helps our customers derive insights that can be translated into concrete solutions. Facilitating our customers’ data-driven decision-making and thus enabling them to act more quickly is at the core of our business model and our success. Does Palantir use customer data for its own purposes? No. We do not use our customers’ data ourselves. We also do not develop and train AI models based on customer data, or reuse customer data in any other way, neither for our own purposes nor for resale to third parties. There are many software companies that offer data analytics in one form or another. What sets Palantir apart from these companies? There are a number of factors that make Palantir unique and different from other software companies. We see our software as an operating system for the modern organization. We offer platforms with extensive analytical functionality and combine this with our industry knowledge of operational processes. But it doesn’t stop at analysis and insights; we believe it is especially important for customers to be able to make better decisions based on comprehensive and verifiable data, both in the field and at the top. We see an organization as the sum of all the decisions it makes. These decisions are interdependent and interrelated in a complex way. We believe it is quite common in organizations that decisions in different departments are made based on siloed data, and that knowledge about these decisions may be unavailable to other departments that could benefit from it. Palantir’s platforms bring order to the data chaos and provide our customers with a common and integrated view of all their relevant data. The result is an interconnected organization that makes better and more sustainable decisions. Building on our longstanding partnerships with some of the world’s most important institutions, our platforms deploy quickly and efficiently for customers. Based on our experience and technology, we can reduce the implementation time from months to days. As mentioned, data protection and data security are fundamental to Palantir and are integrated into our software architecture. We believe that our platforms must not only be able to help our customers comply with current privacy and data protection regulations, but also continuously evolve in line with new legal requirements and expectations in society. In the midst of global uncertainty, it is crucial for our customers to retain localized control over their data to maintain their autonomy. Palantir, as a software as a service (SaaS) vendor, enables its customers to process their most sensitive data within their own borders, whether in the United States, the United Kingdom, or the European Union. This means that for all European customers, any such data integrated in a Palantir platform can be hosted within the EU and will never be transferred outside of the EU. How does Palantir support its customers with data protection? Our longstanding customer relationships include police and intelligence agencies, as well as companies in the health and financial sectors. These are all organizations that operate in highly sensitive and complex digital environments and are subject to strict government requirements. To help them meet their ethical and legal requirements, Palantir has integrated privacy-protective capabilities into our products and continuously developed the software further on these principles. We are committed to helping organizations get value out of their data while protecting sensitive information from misuse and abuse. With our software, the customer can precisely determine data access controls and use. In addition, the customer can determine exactly how long data should be kept. Because a detailed history is kept for the integration and transformation of each data point, the customer can trace when and how data was created or changed. Such versioning within Palantir platforms simplifies reporting and supports compliance with data auditing and retention policies. Our collaboration with the Danish National Police demonstrates how our products enable strict data protection and responsible handling of sensitive information. The Danish National Police selected Palantir through a rigorous, years-long public competition that featured comprehensive data protection requirements. All other competitors eventually dropped out of the competition due to the complexity of these requirements. Within the first year of implementation, even non-technical users within the agency were able to analyze activities on the platform using standard auditing functionality in Palantir’s software. This functionality also makes it possible to identify integrity incidents. The Danish National Police described the partnership with Palantir in the German weekly Die Zeit as the most important acquisition in the history of the Danish police in the field of data protection. Palantir has long been cooperating with police and intelligence services worldwide. Is Palantir a surveillance company? No. Palantir develops software that enables our customers to process their own data legally, securely, and efficiently. We do not engage in surveillance or espionage. Palantir products have unique properties that are of interest to, among other things, intelligence services, but the customer is always obliged to make a legal assessment of the legal use of the software given its authority and purpose. Palantir does not allow the software to be used in violation of any applicable law. What about rumors that Palantir enables predictive policing — is this true? No. Palantir does not provide predictive policing tools. Palantir makes software available to police services worldwide with which they can perform their regular investigative work more efficiently and in accordance with the applicable guidelines and procedures. Why did Palantir offer its services for free during the COVID-19 crisis? In some cases, Palantir has offered its software pro bono in the fight against COVID-19 because we wanted to use our experience, expertise, and software to quickly help with one of the biggest global challenges of the past decades. Palantir has been deployed to various agencies and customers worldwide to support an integrated approach and response to the pandemic. In this way, we have been able to ensure that our customer decision-makers have all relevant information in the fight against COVID-19 in near real time. To give a few examples, our software is currently used by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) in the HHS Protect program and by the National Health Service (NHS) in the UK. With HHS Protect, more than 150 different data sources are collected in one ecosystem. This project integrates data from federal, state and local governments and the health industry to enable a holistic view of the healthcare system. Our system makes it possible to unify and organize such data while the government agencies retain ownership and control over their data. The NHS in the UK has used Foundry to capture and share the demand and supply of protective gear across different institutions in real time. Hospitals could make their individual needs known on a day-to-day basis and in so doing manage the allocation of lifesaving equipment — e.g., ventilators — and optimise the allocation of supplies where patients needed them most. The solution that was developed encompasses a direct integration of already existing systems for managing supplies. This has helped to minimise the administrative burden for NHS employees. Another example we are particularly proud of is how we were able to support The World Food Programme, our partner since 2019, during the pandemic. Humanitarian organizations across the globe utilized WFP’s supply chain to deliver emergency health and humanitarian assistance. With the help of Palantir software, WFP was able to track and update those shipments in real time, delivering more than 148,000 cubic meters of life-saving health and humanitarian cargo to 173 countries on behalf of 72 organizations. Why does Palantir support the GAIA-X initiative, which aims to strengthen Europe’s digital sovereignty? Palantir’s co-founder and CEO, Dr. Alex Karp, has often expressed his admiration for the social market economy in Europe and for the tradition and vast expertise of European industry. At Palantir, we see ourselves as a partner of established European companies and want to support them on the path to digital transformation. An interconnected, secure open data infrastructure that GAIA-X is aiming for will be a major step forward. Since our inception at the turn of the century, we have addressed issues that are also relevant to GAIA-X. For example, how can public and private sector institutions assess the distributed, heterogeneous amounts of data they have collected over decades? How can organizations use data efficiently while collaborating across organizational boundaries without compromising data security and data protection? After more than 17 years of working in highly complex, highly regulated data environments, we have developed an understanding of how technology solutions can be aligned with data management guidelines, legal provisions and other normative preconditions. It is precisely this experience and competence that we want to bring to the GAIA-X project. How does Palantir enable secure collaboration between organizations? Skywise is a great example of how our products enable secure and controlled collaboration within organizations and across organizational boundaries. Skywise is a digital ecosystem for the entire aviation industry, provided by Airbus and powered by Palantir Foundry. Airlines and suppliers in the aviation industry worldwide use Skywise to improve operational efficiency, safety and prevent delays. This allows suppliers to optimize their stocks and reduce late deliveries. Airbus is accelerating the production and development of new business models. Skywise brings different organizations together in one ecosystem. This collaboration is enabled through a unified data integration architecture where the participants can manage their own unified information and collaborate towards a shared purpose by securely exchanging specific data. Would Palantir ever restrict the use of software for ethical reasons? Yes. Palantir has done this on several occasions. For example in an article in the Washington Post (September 2019), our CEO Dr. Alex Karp acknowledges the company’s ethical responsibility to prevent misuse of the technology. Palantir is very aware of the ethical responsibility we have as a company to prevent misuse of our technology. Palantir does not generally work with customers or governments whose positions or actions we consider inconsistent with our mission to support western liberal democracies and their strategic allies. In all cases, we carefully evaluate potential customers and potential uses for adherence to our values and principles. For example, as we make clear in our current public filings with the SEC, Palantir does not do business with the Chinese Communist Party, does not host platforms in China, and imposes restrictions on platform access from China. We also would not provide our software to the Russian government. Palantir has also refused to cooperate with other international government agencies over concerns about human rights violations. Palantir has had a dedicated team dealing with data protection and data ethics issues for many years. Read more about Palantir’s approach to Privacy and Civil Liberties Engineering here. What is it like to work at Palantir? In finding new colleagues, we look for talent everywhere. To get the most out of our software, Palantir needs people from a wide variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and life experiences. We hire former performers, Olympians, opera singers, and nuclear physicists, as much as we hire veterans and industry leaders. We hire graduates, but also people at the top of their field. What unites us as Palantirians is an unwavering passion and dedication to our mission. Wherever you are based, or whatever team you work in, you are part of a group of people who work together to build solutions to the most important problems, in a company that values the very best ideas. This is our engineering culture. If you are excited about working on the world’s most important problems and want the freedom to solve them, we want to work with you. We currently have several vacancies open for our Dutch team. To get you started, view information about the application procedure here. For media inquiries, please email media@palantir.com; to learn more about Palantir platforms, please visit www.palantir.com.

title: Product Design at Palantir: Q&A with the team
description: In this blog post, Product Designers share why they joined Palantir, their day-to-day schedules, advice for potential applicants, and more.
author: Palantir
body: Product Design Palantir Project Management Palantir Culture Teams Product Design at Palantir: Q&A with the team Palantir 8 min read · May 19, 2022 -- 1 Listen Share Press enter or click to view image in full size Product Designers are key members of Palantir product teams. We work on Gotham, Foundry, and Apollo platforms alongside Product Managers and Engineers to define product vision and user experiences. Using design as a communication tool, we ensure that all products shipped convey our mission and reflect our exceptional standards. Product Designers are a force multiplier, helping drive massive impact in product direction and business outcomes, from Palantir’s work with vaccine distribution to counterterrorism. Get Palantir ’s stories in your inbox Join Medium for free to get updates from this writer. Subscribe Subscribe Remember me for faster sign in In this blog post, Product Designers share why they joined Palantir, their day-to-day schedules, advice for potential applicants, and more. Why did you choose to join Palantir? Andy E. (Denver, US) The initial thing that drew me in from the beginning, and now eight years later, was the huge variety of different types of problems within incredibly important domains, everything from national security to healthcare. I still find myself being surprised and intrigued by problems that Palantir is solving. Besides, Palantirians are incredibly humble, driven, and phenomenal critical thinkers. It has really been amazing and humbling to be able to work alongside my teammates here and I’ve learned so much from them. Jiyoung O. (Palo Alto, US) I found Palantir while doing my graduate school thesis on how design can help navigate complex messages, systems, and technologies. I was first attracted by the complex problems that the company deals with and how the products help important institutions use technologies like AI/ML. After watching Palantir’s Gotham and Foundry demo videos and seeing how design contributed to these workflows, I knew Palantir would be a perfect place to apply what I’ve learned! Charles P. (London, UK) I joined Palantir because I wanted to serve people that rely on software to perform some of the world’s most critical workflows. I wanted to bring the high UI standards, which consumer-facing products often have, to mission-driven products and, by doing so, transform the way users understand and interact with software in critical moments. And I knew I could do that at Palantir. In addition, I joined early in my design career and was looking for a place with opportunity for mentorship from talented designers, as well as autonomy. Aashman G. (New York, US) I was initially drawn to the complexity and breadth of the problems I would be able to solve at Palantir. I enjoy working within a relatively flat structure — the best opinion wins, and you are able to forge your own trajectory in the company regardless of your role. Lastly, I was excited to work with an autonomous and multifaceted group of people every day. What’s a typical work day like for you on the design team? Chanel L. (New York, US) I’m often designing for a few projects at a time, each at different phases. For projects that are in implementation phase, I stay up-to-date with teams’ priorities and plans so that I can provide feedback and iterate quickly with my developer teammates. For these projects, the design quality is held at a very high bar. Other projects are in much earlier stages and, in these cases, I act as a strategic partner alongside the product managers, tech leads, and other designers to create vision designs and draft concept primitives to guide discussions. Candice J. (Palo Alto, US) I’m mainly responsible for our geospatial analysis tool on the Gotham platform, and therefore I often think about translating large scale data sets into human-readable information on a map. A typical day for me is comprised of meetings with my team, including engineers and product managers, design presentations, solo design time on projects big and small, as well as progress documentation. Andy E. There’s really no typical day but I would say in general I try to keep my time roughly split into thirds. A third of my time is spent on product development work with our Gotham platform. A second third is spent on new client outreach, and the final third is invested on the Design Team, whether it be mentoring others, planning, or creating growth frameworks for designers. On a typical day, I might help out a designer with a project they’re working on in the morning by providing feedback and ideas, then in the afternoon meet with one of our clients to prototype a concept for a new potential project. There’s a ton of variety and that’s part of what I enjoy. It certainly never gets boring! Aashman G. My workdays come in a few flavors, depending on what I’m working on and where the focus of the broader team is at the time. Some days are primarily for meetings — with users, product teams, and engineers — where we talk through issues, whiteboard, and zoom out to identify big picture goals and next steps. Other days are the opposite, which I use to synthesize signals from meeting-heavy days and design on Figma. There are days I find myself switching context between several projects that vary in scope, which is fun because I start to notice the themes among otherwise distinct work streams and products. Jiyoung O. I usually start my day revisiting the design files from the day before and send them over for feedback as early as possible. Around 10am, I have my team’s daily stand up where we share our work and discuss any coordination needed. Until early afternoon, there are usually a lot of meetings with various partners (product managers, engineers, designers) to receive feedback on the designs I’m working on, get aligned on the direction of a project, or hand over my designs for implementation. I usually spend the rest of my day for some heads down time to digest what I learned from the meetings and iterate on my designs! What is the favorite part about designing at Palantir? Aashman G. I’m attracted to the breadth and complexity of the problems I work on and especially love finding similarities between workflows across different verticals and industries. Data is simply a substrate that facilitates decision making and insight generation for any organization or individual, regardless of whether it’s aerospace data, pharmaceutical data, or financial data. Being able to think about data in an abstract way allows me to draw parallels between how people from different walks of life perform very similar tasks. Candice J. I love the speed at which we can design, build, and ship. It really shined during recent events happening in the world, where we are able to create important tools to aid those in need. It’s a great feeling seeing the positive impact we’ve made through our products. Jiyoung O. The designer’s role at Palantir is not limited to visuals or interactions. Since designers can visualize abstract concepts, we sometimes take part in defining product vision alongside our teammates. Furthermore, designers are user researchers who conduct interviews and gather user feedbacks, and also prototypers who create interactive prototypes to share product vision with clients. I think this wide spectrum of work is my favorite part of being a designer at Palantir. Chanel L. Other designers probably mentioned the big ownership we give to designers and the important missions we support — and both are major drives in my work. However, perhaps a less well known aspect of our design team is the people. Designers at Palantir are thoughtful, humble, and collaborative, and I am constantly inspired by their work. And above all, we build strong friendship within the team and I feel lucky to be supported both at and outside of work. What does growth look like for a Palantir Product Designer? Charles P. The core pillars of growth for designers at Palantir are product ownership, execution, and partnership. Typically, designers take on larger and more complex problems over time. As their scope widens and their expertise deepens, they partner more and more with product leadership to influence the long term vision. That said, growth can take many paths and there is no one size fits all. Growth can also mean pursuing a people leadership role, oriented around growing other designers and fostering a positive culture. Chanel L. One of the first things I learned is to have my own preferences for enabling my success and ability to assist others. This self awareness is a necessary skill that I continue to hone. I learn which design process best compliments not only my strengths but also addresses the task at hand, and the guidance and mentorship I need to overcome my weaknesses. In addition to this self awareness, being proactive also helps me define my growth path at Palantir. Self awareness coupled with proactivity has helped not only me but others on my team to sharpen both our design skills and our soft skills. Candice J. A growth path at Palantir is not linear or easily predictable for any role, including design. We help level up new grad designers to start but it’s really up to individuals to develop continuously in areas of interests and to broaden their ownership. Due to the open culture and flat org structure, anyone can have great impact regardless of level of experience. What excites you about the future of Product Design at Palantir? Aashman G. The design team’s footprint has been growing steadily for several years now and I’m excited to see the snowball effect of the various investments we’ve made into the organization so far. I believe that design at Palantir acts as a multiplier, in that certain actions and interventions by designers have an outsized impact on the product, platform, or company culture. This can largely be attributed to the design superpower of being able to visualize and illustrate complexity in an easily digestible fashion. Charles P. It may sound cliché but I firmly believe we are only at the beginning. Since I joined three years ago, Foundry transformed from a powerful data integration platform into an end-to-end operational system. We’ve developed many primitives in our long history. Now, they serve as stepping stones towards meaningful engagement with different business sectors. New product development and the opportunity for even closer relationships with the business are what excites me about the future of product design at Palantir. Candice J. Many of our previous workflows used to touch one or two of Palantir’s product suite. However, recently we’ve seen a huge expansion of that, where many more products could be used by a single deployment. This means there is more cross collaboration happening between the designers and product teams, and stronger product-driven initiatives and visioning for the future of Palantir. What advice do you have for prospective Palantir design candidates? Jiyoung O. I hope this can help the candidates understand what we look for when hiring new designers: designers at Palantir are very autonomous, meaning we don’t wait for someone to tell us what to do. We actively find out what the problems are, who to talk to for more context, and how to prioritize design solutions. Secondly, designers here are very well rounded. We do everything from research, synthesis, design, to prototyping. Lastly, Palantir designers are great communicators, often presenting designs with a clear story, and they communicate well across various stakeholders. Candice J. I first applied to Palantir as a new grad but didn’t get in and wasn’t sure if I ever would. After gaining a few years of experience, I found out more about myself — what I’m good at and how I wanted to grow. When the opportunity to join Palantir came up again years later, it was a match on both sides, and we’re both happy about the fit. Your career path may not seem clear at the moment but it will eventually all make sense. Keep working on yourself. It’s the best investment you’ll make. Join us and make a difference Palantir Designers solve the most complex problems and we have design opportunities that couldn’t be found anywhere else. If you’d like to make a difference, consider joining us: Product Designer ( New York | London | Denver ) Capture Designer, US Government ( Washington DC ) Product Designer, US Government ( Palo Alto | Washington DC ) Product Designer, New Grad ( New York | London )

title: Palantir Foundry: Supercharge Your BI & Analytics
description: Palantir Foundry does more than work alongside your enterprise business intelligence (BI) and analytics software, it supercharges them.
author: Palantir
body: Palantirtech Business Intelligence Analytics SaaS Foundryarchitecture Palantir Foundry: Supercharge Your BI & Analytics Palantir 6 min read · May 25, 2022 -- 1 Listen Share By Akshay Krishnaswamy , Chief Architect, Palantir Press enter or click to view image in full size Achieving connected operations means going beyond the assembly line approach to data and analytics. It means creating full-fidelity feedback loops between your data, analytics, and operational workflows. Palantir Foundry can help make this possible, first by enriching your existing BI and analytics tooling and then by extending it to include more dynamic decision-making workflows. Step 1: Enrich Your Existing BI Tooling with Foundry Data Integration and Ontology Foundry supercharges your existing BI and analytic tooling with best-in-class data integration and ontology capabilities. Foundry can integrate any existing data assets and models — from massive-scale sensor and IoT sources, telemetry and video data, licensed third-party data, and all internal sources. The Foundry Ontology sits on top of these integrated digital artifacts, using them to formulate a “digital twin” of the real-world things that constitute your business (e.g., plants, customers, transactions). The Ontology acts as a common data layer with multi-modal storage, supporting a diverse range of end-user functionality from search to time series analysis to geospatial visualization and more. Together, these capabilities fortify conventional BI/analytics in several ways: Improve legibility and trust in data. Foundry offers interactive visibility into your data and model pipelines — allowing you to inspect the history of how a particular dataset or piece of logic was generated. The platform automatically traces lineage from raw data all the way to applications where the data is used, eliminating the need to write pipeline lineage documentation that becomes obsolete when things change. As teams make decisions and generate new data on the operational front lines, the Ontology mediates interactions across layers of the stack and ensures that your user application layer can scale without fracturing your core data and model foundation. Incorporate robust security and governance capabilities. While many BI and analytics tools lack integrated security, Foundry offers unified security, lineage, and governance models from source to application. Every data artifact in Foundry can have a permissions and retention policy associated with it. Data administrators can apply governance policies to individual datasets, rows within datasets, folders, projects, and more — reducing the need to fork pipelines and providing a scalable, secure foundation for your BI applications. Embed read-write capabilities into your workflows. The Ontology orchestrates the flow of data, models, and actions across heterogeneous tooling and systems, allowing for continuous learning (discussed more below). Foundry is designed to integrate deeply with your existing BI and analytical tools. It accomplishes this through REST APIs; ODBC and JDBC drivers; Python and R SDKs for connection to data science tools; and out-of-the-box connectors for common tools like Power BI and Tableau. Step 2: Extend Your BI Ecosystem with Interactive Decision-making Applications A fast-changing world demands the ability to pivot from “reactive” to “proactive” decision-making. Technologically, this means giving both technical and non-technical users not just ways to consume insights, but ways to manipulate, analyze, and act on heterogeneous data in dynamic, highly interactive applications. Get Palantir ’s stories in your inbox Join Medium for free to get updates from this writer. Subscribe Subscribe Remember me for faster sign in As a result, we designed Foundry with capabilities that expand the pool of people who can transform data, perform analysis, build models, and build applications — reducing the bottleneck on engineering resources. Quiver is an analytical suite that allows you to plot, transform, and analyze massive-scale time series data and objects. Quiver is backed by time series infrastructure that balances high performance with a sustainable architecture that will scale as data volume and user head count grows, making Foundry both an effective historian and a real-time analytical tool for time series data. Quiver also provides object analysis capabilities to enable users to flexibly create and compare cohorts, perform aggregate analyses across object populations, and analyze object links and relationships. Contour is a point-and-click analysis, transformation, and reporting tool that excels at empowering non-technical users who have ad-hoc top down workflows. Contour allows you to quickly access datasets, conduct common analytical and logical operations in sequence to explore your data, debug data quality, and cleanse and transform your data. All of this can be done at scale — for instance, it allows analysis of large data sets with hundreds of millions of rows. Foundry Reports , Object Explorer , Fusion , and others give users endless options to further analyze and act on integrated data. Beyond these out-of-the-box capabilities, Foundry recognizes that many valuable workflows are highly specific to your organization. To address this, we designed Workshop , a modular application builder that empowers a diverse community of builders to develop and manage complex read-write applications. Press enter or click to view image in full size Workshop marries the configurability of popular BI tools with exquisite dimensionality — backed by Foundry’s data integration and Ontology — that can generally be achieved only through fully custom applications. Workshop lets your teams compose applications using high-quality layouts and dynamic widgets, where builders articulate the inputs, outputs, and actions relevant to their use case. Here are just a few examples of interactive applications configured with Foundry’s modular application building blocks: Manufacturing Bill of Materials Application enables an organization’s raw material purchasing teams to run computations on spot-buy opportunities and calculate how cheaper materials could be utilized within the value chain — all while adjusting parameters like formulation constraints, existing inventory, and forecasted demand. Retail Common Operating Picture allows an organization’s store managers to overlay COVID case information atop retail store sales and operations data — and then adjust inventory and other plans as local case counts change. Airline Flight Alert Inbox shows aircraft swap managers a clear set of alerts on potential disruptions that require triage, review, and action. The inbox includes a detailed view of each individual alert, and action pathways allow users to make decisions on aircraft swaps and trigger changes in operational systems directly from the application. Often, these applications are deployed in hours — fueling rapid concept iteration and saving weeks or months as compared to a fully bespoke solution. By abstracting away technical hurdles such as hosting, authentication, authorization, data integration, monitoring, and more, Workshop greatly reduces development costs and lets you to focus on building. Step 3: Drive Org-Wide Decision-Making Processes While the quality of each BI/analytic application matters, the connectivity of the system as a whole is equally important. Without a smart latticework across tools, organizations may see splintering in their data, logic, and processes — and in turn slowing progress in their ability to adapt to new conditions and improve. To deliver deep operational connectivity across your BI, analytics, and operational tooling, Foundry employs an approach called decision orchestration. While conventional BI and analytics lack dynamic decision-based workflows, Foundry’s decision orchestration layer captures decisions made in user-facing applications and writes the results back into the organization’s Ontology, creating the feedback loops needed for high-velocity organizational learning. Importantly, we designed Foundry so that it does not simply record past decisions, but actually enables you to simulate possible future states of the world. By leveraging Ontology-backed applications, decision makers can perform “what-if” analysis and scenario-test the downstream consequences of actions to better determine how they contribute to global business priorities. Press enter or click to view image in full size 1) Foundry digitally represents the chain of logistical, physical, and logical flows across organizational units and models how operations are functioning in near real-time. (2) Users can perform “what-if” analysis and simulate the downstream consequences of possible actions to better determine how decisions contribute to global business priorities. (3) When operators make decisions, the platform records the outcomes: which decisions were right, how they could have been better, and why they were made. This feedback loop allows the platform to continuously improve decisions and recommendations over time in alignment with global strategy. To run these simulations, the Foundry Ontology blends inputs from integrated data and models, systems of action, and more. The platform then captures any decisions, results, and relevant context back into the Ontology as well as to underlying systems of action (e.g., ERP, CRM, MES, Asset Config, Edge). This operational feedback informs future simulations, improves data and AI/ML models, fuels higher-level decision-making, and accelerates learning within the organization. See What Foundry Can Do For Your BI & Analytics Processes Learn more about the Foundry BI & Analytics suite here . Learn more about the Foundry integration with popular SQL and BI tools here . Get in touch with a member of our Foundry product team to learn more about how Foundry can enhance your BI and Analytics tooling.

title: Raising Kids While Raising a Career in Tech
description: Hear about Marina Miller's journey and growth as both a mother and a woman in tech at Palantir.
author: Palantir
body: Motherhood Tech Palantir Palantir Culture Careers Raising Kids While Raising a Career in Tech Palantir 8 min read · May 26, 2022 -- Listen Share Press enter or click to view image in full size I’m Marina Miller , and I’m one of the Group Leads of the Production Infrastructure department. Since joining Palantir in 2012, it’s been a wild ride both as a growing leader in tech and as a mother. There were many hills to climb and moments of doubt. Among them, there were also opportunities to take on something impactful, something hard, and something that I wasn’t sure I would succeed at, especially with kids. And yet, today and throughout my career as working mother, I have a seat at the table. My ideas are heard and I feel excited bringing my strengths to my group, my colleagues. I am thriving as both a leader and a working mother. My journey may look different from yours, and while Palantir gave me the support and latitude to “have it all” — career growth and being the parent I want to be, I know this unfortunately isn’t the case for all working mothers. I had to have uncomfortable conversations and lean on outstanding colleagues. I’ve certainly benefited from inherent privileges that I will not attempt to disguise as anything but luck. I hope my story and the lessons I’ve learned serve as encouragement and support for your growth, wherever you may be. Becoming a working mom Transitioning to life as a working mom was scary and filled with doubts. That’s completely natural. Colleagues should be there to both affirm concerns you may have, and support you through addressing them. When I joined Palantir almost a decade ago, I took on a role as a Deployment Strategist. This included traveling almost 100% of the time, because I wanted to work in our government space in DC while staying close to family in New Jersey. I was (and still am!) incredibly motivated by our mission — at the time I got to work with some of the largest and most critical US government institutions that were using Palantir’s Gotham platform on high-profile terrorism cases and solving mortgage-backed securities fraud rings. It was exhilarating, and I felt my personal mark on making our world a better and safer place. In 2016, I gave birth to my son and took over 20 weeks of fully paid maternity leave. It was a true maternity leave — I didn’t have to hop on work calls, and instead spent the full 20 weeks both enjoying my newborn and adjusting to the challenges of being a new mother. Yet as my maternity leave came to a close, some doubt began to creep in. I began to think through how being a mother would affect my impact and growth in my career. Wanting to be home, I knew I wouldn’t be able to travel for government work. Would I be sidelined to a project that didn’t excite me? Would I still have access to the same growth I experienced over the past 4 years? Would I be able to find my footing with colleagues outside the government space? Fortunately, my doubts were quickly mitigated; on my first day back, my lead at the time (Keyur P. also a parent), enthusiastically asked 100 questions about baby sleep, balancing time with my spouse, and silly baby sounds. At the same time, he acknowledged my fears and encouraged me to talk to people working on different projects at Palantir. He reminded me that my strengths and skillsets, my goal orientation, human EQ, and execution power, were transferrable to many problems the company worked on. He gave me confidence and reminded me to be open to opportunities that may seem outside my comfort zone, that would continue to accelerate my growth instead of stifling it. That opportunity came in the form of a colleague encouraging me to take on a role as the head of our internal data team. I went from having doubts of finding my footing again to suddenly leading an organization. It was completely out of my comfort zone and again I wondered, could I learn and excel at what felt like a completely new area? Would I be able to focus when I was sleep deprived, missing my baby and reluctantly leaving him with a new caregiver? Support + Discovery = Growth Learning to be a working mother, while at the same time learning to build a team, presented challenges. Being supported by Palantir meant being supported in both pursuits — not only having my needs as a mother met, but also being fully empowered to pursue new growth opportunities. Though having affirmation from my team was critically important, feeling supported by the company was priceless. I was welcomed by other mothers at Palantir and was set up with brand new pumping equipment, as well as a beautiful purpose-built mother’s room. I was encouraged to set up my calendar with pumping breaks, time commuting, and “baby time.” Every single person up to the executive level respected those blocks. So far, so good! Get Palantir ’s stories in your inbox Join Medium for free to get updates from this writer. Subscribe Subscribe Remember me for faster sign in As I successfully got more and more responsibility in my role leading the data team, I found myself learning things I never imagined I was capable of — I was working on teaching our internal teams (across finance, recruiting, events, and more) to leverage Foundry for internal company operations while also successfully leading a group of very technical data engineers, despite not being an engineer myself. I grew my capacity to be a leader for my team. I mentored employees that felt they had stagnated in their careers to be more impactful. I did all of that while still managing to get home to my son and spend quality time with him every day. As the success of this team grew and took off, Palantir asked me to speak at our company-wide Hobbitcon event on some of the compelling success our team was bringing to the company. This was an exciting opportunity to share the impactful work my team was doing. However, Hobbitcon was being held in California, while my spouse would be on work-related travel. Rather than taking the opportunity away, Palantir helped accommodate my talk to be a remote one, with my face broadcast on a large screen to a live audience. It was the first time I felt confident it was possible to both grow in my career and be the present parent I strived to be. Later, I decided I was ready to travel again — occasionally to our London and Palo Alto offices to work and connect with various team members. Again, there were a lot of logistical questions on how I could do this between childcare and pumping. Palantir provided the Milk Stork service to me at no cost to make the process as seamless as possible. Being supported was more than the services and resources, but how they were put in place to help fuel my growth! Realizing my growth was exponential Being supported as a mother enabled me to realize my potential and grow my team. My growth in turn ended up being great for the business! From here, a trusted colleague (the same one that encouraged me to join the data team!) asked me to take on a new, more complicated team — our cloud team. This team was bigger than the data team, and the subject matter was completely foreign to me. I was also nervous, because I was pregnant with my second child, and wasn’t sure if the team would want someone that would be out on leave in 9 months. I openly shared this with my colleague, who was thrilled by the news and more invested than ever in my success. Palantir again supported me by ensuring I could take an AWS course and exam to learn as quickly as I could. My lead and mentors continuously reminded me and encouraged me that I had the skills to succeed here, and gave me the confidence to jump in and execute. I did it, and this time I realized there was not a ceiling to what I could do and to how much growth Palantir was willing to invest in for my career. When my daughter was born in 2018, upon return from my second maternity leave and almost 6 months later, I was again nervous. Would I return to the same team, where one of my direct reports was running the team in my place in the interim? How would I again have an impact even bigger than before while juggling two kids? Quelling my fears almost instantly, two group leads of the Production Infrastructure department, Greg D. and Brian K. (appreciate you both!), invited me to help scale their organization — leveraging the same skills they saw me leverage with previous teams. Upon the encouragement of my new lead, Maggie A. (not a parent, but also a woman who was deeply invested in my growth) I accepted their proposal under the condition I would be promoted to a group lead along with them — and they said yes! As I write about this experience in hindsight, it feels like I had the unwavering support of my lead and colleagues. That said, it’s important to note this portion of my career required multiple “uncomfortable” conversations. I had to advocate for myself, create a role that did not exist for other non-engineers at the time, and really put myself out there on behalf of my career and parenting goals. These moments tested my self-confidence, and I often felt my heart racing outside of my body as I forced myself to speak up. Success here truly required a partnership — internally with myself along with trusted mentors who believed in me. The journey from here was wild. Together we grew the department from 30 people to over 100. I took on recruiting, resourcing and various operational challenges I had never experienced. To date, my role as a group lead in Production Infrastructure sometimes feels like running a startup — the access to problems, the opportunity to innovate and learn the infrastructure space has been incredible. Doing it successfully while raising two small humans (ages 6 and 3 at the time of writing) during COVID is not something I could have done at any other company. Finding a community In addition to my growth, I’ve also developed a strong network of other mothers that are leaders at Palantir. The head of our major internal operations team, the head of our commercial business and more. All of these women are part of Palantir’s mother affinity group and are both official and unofficial resources to me. We often connect on existing challenges we are experiencing — how to balance a COVID quarantine with a critical business deadline, how to best use Palantir’s care.com benefit to find a new caregiver, and how to support other new working moms at Palantir. Because of how valuable this network has been to me, I’ve also in turn invested in ensuring such a network exists in Production Infrastructure. When I started in the org in 2018, I was one of three women in the department, and the only mother. As of January 2022, the department has 15 women, most of which are leading teams — including another working mom and parents on every team. Palantir has certainly come a long way in how we take care of our parents. There were certainly road bumps and lessons along the way, but I’m proud of where we’ve ended up, and the direction we’re taking forward. The tech industry as a whole is still undergoing that journey, as businesses continue to (hopefully) learn and improve on how to provide for their employees. I, for one, am looking forward to having more working mothers on our in Production Infrastructure organization, as well as growing the parent community at Palantir. Check out our open roles here and join me if what I’ve shared is something you care about too.

title: Palantir’s Commitment to Compliance: ISO 9001
description: Palantir implements stringent compliance standards across some of the most highly regulated industries while addressing their most critical problems, without losing momentum.
author: Palantir
body: Palantirtech Palantirinfosec Iso Iso9001 Infosec Palantir’s Commitment to Compliance: ISO 9001 Palantir 3 min read · May 31, 2022 -- Listen Share Press enter or click to view image in full size There is a common misconception that regulatory frameworks hinder companies from iterating at the speed necessary to succeed. At Palantir, we don’t have that option. Compliance is integral to our success. Palantir implements stringent compliance standards across some of the most highly regulated industries while addressing their most critical problems, without losing momentum. Palantir is proud to announce we have successfully completed our ISO 9001 certification as of April 1, 2022. ISO 9001 is defined as the international standard that specifies requirements for a Quality Management System (QMS). Organizations use the standard to demonstrate the ability to consistently provide products and/or services that meet customer and regulatory requirements. Palantir pursued ISO 9001 to demonstrate our structure, planning, processes, and resources are aligned and compliant. While this accomplishment often comes by sacrificing speed and efficiency, we achieved compliance while maintaining the same product iteration velocity. This certification validates the processes that support our longstanding pursuit of continuous improvement and quality. For a copy of Palantir’s ISO 9001 certificate, please visit our Safebase Trust and Security Portal . The portal can be used to explore Palantir’s security controls, accreditations, and compliance of our software products. For additional questions, please reach out to your Palantir representative. Get Palantir ’s stories in your inbox Join Medium for free to get updates from this writer. Subscribe Subscribe Remember me for faster sign in There are three critical elements that enabled us to pursue and obtain ISO 9001 while maintaining our continuous integration/continuous deployment (CI/CD) product delivery practices: Customer focus. We send our engineers into the field to work directly with our customers — configuring our products, helping them integrate their data, optimizing their workflows, and producing operational results in weeks, not years. By establishing a true partnership, we help customers get the most out of our products and engineering expertise. This partnership means we have the feedback loop already established to continue to improve the quality of our products. Because of this, we had the data and process we needed to align with the “Customer Focus” and “Engagement of People” ISO 9001 quality principals. ISO 27001 Program. Palantir had already established an Information Security Management System (ISMS) through our ISO 27001 certification. The ISMS helps drive many critical components that relate to ISO 9001 — such as risk oversight, metrics to support measurement and monitoring, and a successful audit program. Palantir’s Technical Compliance team was able to leverage these processes to align with the “Process Approach” ISO 9001 quality principal. Apollo. Apollo is the true champion for ISO 9001. Apollo manages and safely deploys our Gotham and Foundry platforms . Each platform is made up of hundreds of individual microservices, each owned by a development team that writes and releases product features independently. This approach allows us to roll out updates across services asynchronously, increasing feature velocity. However, this type of microservice architecture traditionally makes the deployment and quality management of the software more complex. Apollo automates this complexity away. It is configured to understand what to upgrade, when to do it, and how. It upholds change management standards to ensure quality and availability while continuously deploying safe and verified services to our product fleet. Apollo enables Palantir to meet the “Engagement of People,” “Process Approach,” “Improvement,” and “Evidence-based Decision Making” ISO 9001 quality principles. With Apollo, Palantir deploys a minimum of 80,000 updates each week to existing Foundry and Gotham customers, at no additional cost to them. This is driven by one centralized operations team. Apollo’s assurance of strict quality and compliance while maintaining true continuous deployment keeps our customers, developers, and quality team happy. Palantir is excited to continue expanding and growing our compliance program. Our QMS has grown into a mature process and achieving the ISO 9001:2015 certification is a strong step forward in creating a framework under which we can continue to sustain excellence and pursue further improvements.

title: Democratizing Security Detection
description: Security detection programs face significant scaling challenges. This post shares Palantir's learnings and suggests actionable detection strategies.
author: Palantir
body: Palantirtech Palantirinfosec Infosec Security Securitydetection Democratizing Security Detection Palantir 13 min read · Jun 2, 2022 -- 1 Listen Share Press enter or click to view image in full size Introduction Security detection programs face significant scaling challenges. As the size and scope of an organization grows, so too do the volume and diversity of security alerts; this influx can result in adverse impacts to an organization’s security posture, and may cause burnout among security staff responsible for triaging alerts. Teams often try to address their alerting volume by adding more personnel, but simply increasing headcount is an unsustainable long-term solution. At Palantir, we have over 3,000 employees and contractors working around the globe. We run a diverse enterprise ecosystem with hundreds of applications across tens of thousands of hosts. We also provide Palantir software-as-a-service across hyperscale cloud providers including Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, and Google Compute. Despite Palantir’s relatively complex technical infrastructure, all information security monitoring, alert triage, and incident response across this infrastructure is centralized and managed by a team of fewer than 10 people. The goal of this blog post is twofold: First, to share our learnings on scaling our detection program through democratization of security alerts Second, to provide actionable detection strategies that should be considered in most environments. Detection Architecture Before we dive in to democratizing security detection, let’s discuss our detection architecture. This will vary considerably between organizations, but the base elements are similar. The Palantir Computer Incident Response Team (CIRT) is responsible for all facets of security detection and response across the enterprise. This includes detection on hosts, networks, applications, and cloud infrastructure. On the log source side, the CIRT defines all telemetry requirements and sources. They are the final say in validating and approving telemetry sources based upon the utility of security-relevant logs and data. Security-relevant logs and data are plumbed via hundreds of log pipelines into a centralized security information and event management (SIEM) platform. The CIRT then develops alerting and detection strategies (ADS) to surface unusual or malicious activity across these data sources. Generated alerts then flow into our security orchestration, automation, and response (SOAR) platform. Depending on the alert, we apply code playbooks to perform specific actions based upon the source, context, and payload of the alert. One subset of these code playbooks are used for identifying and responding to security events through user security awareness and triage. InfoSecBot InfoSecBot is an application integration between our SOAR platform and our Slack tenant, and is our most successful implementation of surfacing unusual activity directly to users. We have been running InfoSecBot in production across our company since 2016 and the capabilities, features, and scope have only increased over time. There are several key operations handled by InfoSecBot. These are implemented as modules in our SOAR platform, and the ADS author can select one or more modules as they are developing and implementing an alert. These modules include: Individual Notify: Notifying a user via direct message (DM) with an arbitrary alert payload. Individual Challenge: Challenging a user via direct message (DM) with an arbitrary alert payload. A challenge consists of a message and a confirm/deny button to collect their response. Group Notify : Notifying a slack channel via a message with an arbitrary alert payload. Group Challenge : Challenging a slack channel via a message with an arbitrary alert payload. A challenge consists of a message and a confirm/deny button to collect their response. MFA Challenge : Issuing a Duo multi-factor authentication prompt to collect a response from a user. These modules can be chained together to construct complex detection workflows. For example, an alert is presented to an individual user via direct message. They are given a challenge and have 15 minutes to confirm or deny via a Slack button. The user clicks confirm, but, due to the severity of the alert, a Duo multi-factor authentication prompt is issued to confirm their identity. Once the Duo prompt has been approved, the alert may be closed, de-escalated in priority, or surfaced to the CIRT for manual validation. Had the user clicked the deny button, the timeout expired, or the Duo prompt failed, the alert would have immediately escalated and other automation would have kicked in. Detection Opportunities and Strategies While there is a real cost of time and attention when surfacing these alerts to users, it provides some of the strongest signal possible, and dramatically reduces time-to-response for unusual or unauthorized activity. Additionally, depending on the efficacy and severity of an alert, additional automation can be incorporated in response to user signal, including password resets, account lockouts, token revocation, or device quarantining and isolation. The following sections of this publication include a sampling of the alerting & detection strategies that shoulder a significant portion of our overall alert volume. By deconflicting high-volume alerts directly with the operating party, these strategies have allowed the CIRT to expand its attack surface coverage without proportionally adding to our headcount. We encourage other organizations to develop their own unique ADS and find a mechanism to share them with the broader InfoSec community. While there are operational security considerations around publicly acknowledging and documenting internal alerts, we hope these examples spur greater sharing and collaboration, inspire detection enhancements for other defenders, and ultimately increase the operational cost for attackers. Detecting Account Takeover Account takeover can be quickly detected in response to unusual activity impacting user account primitives. Users have direct knowledge of major actions they’ve performed with their account, especially if you can reach them within a short window of time after the behavior occurs. The following detection strategies are designed to help surface attacks using account takeover techniques. Detecting Account Takeover: Failed MFA — A User Rejects or Disavows an MFA Prompt Attack Summary: An attacker ascertains the password of a user, and attempts to authenticate as that user. However, due to MFA, the attacker is unable to authenticate without the user’s second factor of authentication. Detection Strategy: MFA is often touted as a control to harden one’s posture against account takeover. However, in addition to being a hardening control, we believe that MFA should also serve as a basis for alerting & detection. Any MFA prompt denied by a user ought to be treated as a case of potential account takeover, and should generate a corresponding alert. Response: When a user (or an actor attempting to authenticate as a user) attempts to log in, they’ll receive an MFA notification; the user can choose to either accept, or reject that notification. If a user denies an MFA prompt, an alert will propagate to the CIRT’s alerting & detection pipeline, and an analyst will review the activity in question. Detecting Account Takeover: User Authenticates to a Sensitive Resource Attack Summary: An attacker takes over a victim account for the purposes of using the victim’s access to a sensitive target resource. Detection Strategy: Monitor security / audit logs for discrete authentication events against sensitive platforms, hosts, or resources. Response: An InfoSecBot direct message notification is issued to the user whenever they authenticate to an in-scope resource; the message includes: A timestamp of the activity. The resource to which their account authenticated. The IP address from which the authentication attempt was initiated. The user in question must affirmatively respond to the InfoSecBot message prompt, and must additionally confirm an MFA prompt from InfoSecBot. If the user fails to complete the prompt / MFA, the alert will be escalated to the CIRT. Detecting Credential Resets Passwords are horrible things; they’re often weak or re-used, and it’s all too easy to hand a password over to an attacker . However, until passwordless authentication is ubiquitous, passwords are a necessary evil. The following detection strategies are designed to help surface attacks using credential reset techniques. Detecting Credential Resets: User changes their password Attack Summary: A compromised user may attempt to rotate their credentials to gain exclusive access to the account. Detection Strategy: Monitor security logs (e.g. AzureAD, Okta, Windows Event Logs) for discrete user-initiated password change workflows. Response: An InfoSecBot direct message notification is issued to the user whenever they perform a password change on their enterprise accounts. The alert payload presented includes: A timestamp of the activity. The origin of their password rotation, including device hostname and IP address. In the event the activity is unexpected or unusual, the user is given instructions on how to quickly surface it to the CIRT. Detecting Credential Resets: User has their password changed by an administrator Attack Summary: A compromised user with elevated permissions may attempt to perform a credential reset on another account to move laterally, or to privilege escalate. Detection Strategy: Monitor security logs (e.g. AzureAD, Okta, Windows Event Logs) for discrete administrator-initiated password change workflows. Response: An InfoSecBot direct message notification is issued to the user whenever a password is forcibly changed by an administrator for their enterprise accounts. The alert payload presented includes: A timestamp of the activity. The origin of their password rotation, including device hostname and IP address. The username of the administrator. In the event the activity is unexpected or unusual, the user is given instructions on how to quickly surface it to the CIRT. The response strategy may be extended to include notifying the administrator that they performed this action. This provides additional detection properties, and acts as an oversight mechanism for users with privileged access. Detecting Credential Resets: User has a passwordless bypass code created for them Passwordless authentication ideally leverages hardware security tokens. However, users may lose or forget their security tokens, preventing access to information systems. Additionally, users need to initially enroll their security tokens before they can start using them. To enable these workflows, bypass codes or temporary access passes may need to be handed to users. These effectively function as both the first and second factor of authentication for users, and are typically time-bound or limited in usage. Attack Summary: A compromised user with elevated permissions may attempt to create a bypass code or temporary access pass for a user. Detection Strategy: Monitor security logs (e.g. AzureAD, Okta, Windows Event Logs) for discrete administrator-initiated bypass code creation or association workflows. Response: An InfoSecBot direct message notification is issued to the user whenever a password is forcibly changed by an administrator for their enterprise accounts. The alert payload presented includes: A timestamp of the activity. Details regarding the bypass code or temporary access pass. The username of the administrator. In the event the activity is unexpected or unusual, the user is given instructions on how to quickly surface it to the CIRT. The response strategy may be extended to include notifying the administrator that they performed this action. This provides additional detection properties, and acts as an oversight mechanism for users with privileged access. Detecting Credential Resets: User attempts password recovery. For security reasons, we do not allow self-service password recovery. However, this is a very common technique abused by attackers to gain initial access to a legitimate account. Get Palantir ’s stories in your inbox Join Medium for free to get updates from this writer. Subscribe Subscribe Remember me for faster sign in Attack Summary: An attacker abuses a self-service password recovery portal to gain initial access to an account. Detection Strategy: Monitor security logs (e.g. AzureAD, Okta, Windows Event Logs) for discrete user-initiated password recovery attempts. Response: An InfoSecBot direct message notification is issued to the user whenever a password reset request occurs. The alert payload presented includes: A timestamp of the activity. The origin of the password recovery process, including device hostname and IP address. Whether the password recovery process was successful or not. In the event the activity is unexpected or unusual, the user is given instructions on how to quickly surface it to the CIRT. If self-service password recovery is enabled, multiple failed attempts can be a high-signal detection. However, an attacker may get lucky with their first attempt, so mandatory notification to impacted users is appropriate. Detecting Credential Phishing In recognition of passwords (and the human behavior derivative of passwords) being arguably the weakest link in one’s identity security posture, Palantir’s InfoSec staff sought to build a dedicated tool to augment our approach to combatting credential phishing & re-use. The result was our browser extension “PhishCatch”, which has since been open sourced; Read more about PhishCatch’s functionality, and its role at Palantir on GitHub , or on our blog . Palantir’s PhishCatch alerting & detection works as follows: Detection Credential Phishing: PhishCatch Alerting If / when a user inputs their password on a page other than Palantir’s dedicated IDP, PhishCatch will create an alert. The PhishCatch alert will then propagate to the CIRT’s SOAR, at which point a series of automation will run against the alert: InfoSecBot will Slack the user with a request to change their password; this message will repeat every hour for 72 hours.
